blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge. Modern pipelines combine embedding, chunking, retrieval, reranking, query augmentation, context compression, and agentic verification, yet these techniques are typically evaluated one at a time. It remains unclear whether their isolated gains survive composition, whether retrieval quality and answer faithfulness favor the same design choices, and whether conclusions from small corpora hold at large scale. We pre-declare three hypotheses and introduce LASAGNA, an open-source framework for controlled RAG evaluation. We test 450 configurations across eight benchmarks and corpora ranging from 5K to 200K documents. Three findings emerge. First, individually strong techniques from different phases of a RAG pipeline do not necessarily compose: three retrieval techniques predict a +47% combined improvement but deliver only +17% when used together. Second, component gains stack differently for retrieval and faithfulness, and optimizing one can hurt the other. Third, the best composition changes as the corpus grows: the combination that wins on a small corpus may not remain best at large scale. These findings show that gains measured in isolation are not reliable predictors of realistic performance, and that new RAG techniques should be tested with the full surrounding stack. We call on researchers to do so and supply LASAGNA to simplify these experiments.
blocks.zh: 检索增强生成(RAG)将大型语言模型作为外部知识的基础. 现代管道结合了嵌入,分块,取回,再排位,查询增强,上下文压缩,和代理验证,然而这些技术通常一次被评价一次. 仍然不清楚的是,它们的孤立收益是否在组成中存活下来,检索质量和回答忠诚度是否倾向于相同的设计选择,以及小公司的结论是否具有大规模。 我们预先宣布了三个假设,并引入了LASAGNA,一个用于控制下RAG评价的开源框架. 我们通过8个基准测试450个配置,以及5K至200K文件。 得出了三个结论。 第一,来自RAG管道不同阶段的个别强能技术不一定构成:三种检索技术预测一个+47%的综合改进,但在一起使用时只提供+17%。 第二,组件增益堆栈不同,用于取回和取信,优化一个可以伤害另一个. 第三,随着实体的增多,最佳的构成发生变化:在小实体上取胜的组合可能无法保持大规模的最佳组合。 这些调查结果表明,孤立地测量的增益并不是对现实性能的可靠预测,新的RAG技术应该用完整的周边堆栈进行测试. 我们呼吁研究人员这样做,并提供LASAGNA来简化这些实验.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Retrieval-augmented generation
(RAG) ( Gao et al., 2023b ; Fan et al., 2024 ) combines choices across
many pipeline stages. Our study covers eight stages that span the
dominant design axes in modern RAG ( Fig. 1 b; full
catalog in Appendix K ): embedding, chunking, index-time
enrichment, retrieval, query augmentation, reranking, context
compression, and agentic quality gates. Most new techniques are
proposed and evaluated one stage at a time, in isolation from the
surrounding pipeline, or from several representative pipelines that
would test whether findings generalize ( Yu et al., 2024 ) . Adding to the complexity, RAG systems
are evaluated for two goals ( Saad-Falcon et al., 2024 ; Friel et al., 2024 ) :
retrieving the right content (NDCG@10) and producing a faithful
answer from it ( Es et al., 2024 , RAGAS;) . It is unclear whether isolated gains persist under composition. It
is also unclear whether the same design choices optimize both
retrieval quality (which documents are retrieved) and answer
faithfulness (whether the answer is grounded in those documents),
two goals RAG evaluation typically reports separately. We pre-declare three hypotheses. H1. Components often fail
to compose: isolated gains from single-component ablations do not
necessarily persist when components are combined. H2. A
simple RAG pipeline can be near-optimal in many settings, while
more elaborate configurations tend to specialize to narrower ones.
Most RAG ablations in the literature run at 5K to 50K documents,
whereas the applications RAG can serve run at corpora an order of
magnitude larger; H3. composition rankings shift with
corpus scale, so conclusions from small-corpus benchmarks may not
hold at larger scales. Prior work has explored combinations through
configuration sweeps and heuristic
search ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025 ; Rau et al., 2024 ; Jin et al., 2025 ; Kim et al., 2024 ; Fu et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2026 ) ; these
approaches can identify strong configurations but do not directly
measure interaction effects: whether the benefit of one component
depends on the other components in the pipeline. These interactions,
and how they change with corpus scale, remain largely unquantified.

blocks.en:
Testing these hypotheses requires a framework that isolates pipeline
stages and supports reproducible evaluation across benchmarks. We
created lasagna , an open-source RAG framework, to provide
this ( Fig. 1a , Section 3 ). Each
stage sits behind a fixed interface, so swapping one method cannot
silently change the implementation at another. Adding a new
technique is a single line of code; the framework tests it inside a
complete modern pipeline without reimplementing the surrounding stack.

blocks.en:
We use lasagna to study RAG composition with a
167-configuration D-optimal
design ( Fedorov et al., 1972 ; Atkinson et al., 2007 ) across eight
configurable stages of a modern RAG pipeline
( Table 10 ), eight benchmarks ( Fig. 5 ),
and corpus sizes from 5K to 200K documents, complemented by 138
non-factorial ablation configurations across 24 targeted
experiments ( Appendix F ). Across the factorial, ablation suite, and scaling sweep, the
central finding is that techniques that perform well separately do
not consistently retain their gains inside a full pipeline, and the
pattern differs between retrieval and faithfulness. Retrieval gains
compose sub-additively: the three largest single-component
improvements sum to a predicted + 47 % +47\% NDCG@10 gain, but the
composed pipeline realizes only + 17 % +17\% ( Section D.14 ).
Faithfulness gains compose near-additively: separately measured
improvements approximately transfer to the full pipeline
( Table 47 ). Pipeline and generator
also partly substitute: a stronger generator helps the lightest pipeline
far more than the heaviest, so a heavier stack buys
less when the generator is already strong ( Section F.9 ).

blocks.en:
Three practical implications follow. First, the components that
improve retrieval are not the same as those that improve faithfulness,
and optimizing one metric can hurt the other. Second, the four
complete RAG profiles expose a Pareto tradeoff on retrieval
quality, faithfulness, and response time, with no universal winner.
Adding an agentic loop to a strong retrieval stack yields only a
negligible faithfulness gain while hurting retrieval quality and
latency. Across three other benchmarks at 100K–200K documents,
lighter pipelines retain similar measured quality at 10 10 – 20 × 20\times lower latency
( Sections 5 and D.8 ). Third, corpus
size shifts profile rankings: the design leading at small corpora
trails by 13.7 % 13.7\% NDCG@10 at 200K, with a rank flip visible from
25K ( Fig. 4(a) ). Small-corpus rankings should therefore
be rechecked at the intended scale.
Our contributions are:

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Modern RAG spans a layered design space with plausible interaction
points at every stage (full method catalog in Appendix K ).
On retrieval , sparse baselines
(BM25 ( Robertson & Zaragoza, 2009 ) ) coexist with dense encoders
(BGE-M3 ( Chen et al., 2024a ) , E5 ( Wang et al., 2022 ) ), learned
sparse encoders (SPLADE ( Formal et al., 2021 ) ), and
late-interaction models (ColBERT ( Khattab & Zaharia, 2020 ) ), fused
by reciprocal-rank fusion (RRF) ( Cormack et al., 2009 ) or learned
hybrids. Reranking spans cross-encoder scorers trained on
MS-MARCO ( Nogueira & Cho, 2019 ) , ensemble rerankers, and
diversity-driven selection (MMR; Carbonell & Goldstein, 1998 ). Context
compression is either token-budget aware
(LLMLingua ( Jiang et al., 2023a ) ) or positional
(lost-in-the-middle-aware selection ( Liu et al., 2024 ) ). Query augmentation rewrites the query before retrieval:
HyDE ( Gao et al., 2023a ) drafts a hypothetical answer,
RAG-Fusion ( Rackauckas, 2024 ) fans out multi-query
variants, decomposition ( Khattab et al., 2024 ) splits multi-hop
questions into sub-questions, and step-back
prompting ( Zheng et al., 2024 ) abstracts before retrieving. Index-time processing enriches chunks before retrieval with
document summaries (RAPTOR ( Sarthi et al., 2024 ) ), contextual
prefixes ( Anthropic, 2024 ) , or entity-graph indexes
(GraphRAG ( Edge et al., 2024 ) ). Generation-time control adds correction and gating loops around the answer model
(CRAG ( Yan et al., 2024 ) , Self-RAG ( Asai et al., 2024 ) ,
Speculative-RAG ( Wang et al., 2025 ) ). Each of these
stages has been shown to help in isolation on some benchmark, but
they compose along more edges than a single-component ablation can
enumerate. We study how these choices combine once
deployed together, and lasagna lets others ask
compositionality questions in the same environment by
registering a new component and evaluating it against a full modern
pipeline.

blocks.en:
Table 1 positions lasagna against prior
work that studies RAG beyond isolated components. Best-practice
studies ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Barnett et al., 2024 ) search greedily
for strong end-to-end configurations but do not estimate interaction
effects. Benchmarking libraries such as BERGEN ( Rau et al., 2024 ) and FlashRAG ( Jin et al., 2025 ) support composition in a shared
codebase but do not enforce the stage isolation that controlled
interaction estimation requires, so measured differences cannot be
cleanly attributed to the component being varied
(a positional smoke run against both is reported in Section G.4 ). Automated
configuration search ( Kim et al., 2024 ) optimizes
over configurations but reports only the winning setting, not the
interaction structure that produced it, so the resulting guidance
does not transfer when any assumption changes. Evaluation
suites ( Krishna et al., 2025 ) and domain
benchmarks ( Xiong et al., 2024 ) supply metrics
and tasks but not a common pipeline in which those metrics can be
compared across controlled compositions. Generation-time
controls ( Yan et al., 2024 ) strengthen the agentic layer but are
usually tested with retrieval fixed, leaving composition with a tuned
stack untested.

blocks.en: 3 LASAGNA: A Compositional Framework for RAG
blocks.zh: 3 RAGNA: RAG的组成框架

blocks.en:
lasagna is an open-source framework for
evaluating new RAG components inside a complete modern pipeline.
A researcher proposing a new reranker, chunker, or agentic loop today
must either compare against a stripped-down baseline that does not
reflect a modern pipeline, or reimplement the surrounding stack. The
first biases the conclusion by mixing implementation differences
with algorithmic ones; the second is prohibitively expensive and
rarely attempted. lasagna provides a configurable
end-to-end pipeline ( Fig. 1a ) with a fixed
interface per stage that the framework enforces, so a new component
drops into one stage and is measured against the same surrounding
stack used by every reported configuration (full code patterns in Sections H.2.2 , H.2.3 and H.2.4 ).
The workflow spans nine processing stages: document processing,
chunking, index-time enrichment, embedding and indexing, query
augmentation, retrieval, reranking, context compression, and answer
generation with optional agentic verification.
Every pipeline component is a subclass of a typed abstract base class:
eight component types are supported ( embedder , chunker , reranker , retriever , document_processor , query_enhancer , agentic_pipeline , and generator ), each
stage’s inputs and outputs are typed dataclass contracts, and
behavioral tests check that swapping one implementation does not mutate
a neighboring stage’s state. A single @registry.register("<stage>", "<name>") decorator suffices
to make a new component discoverable at YAML-config time.
The framework ships with 53 built-in components, the 30 methods across the eight factorial
dimensions ( Table 10 ; full catalog in Appendix K ),
six vector backends (Milvus, Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, pgvector,
OpenSearch), and adapters for the eight benchmarks used here (five
BEIR retrieval sets and three long-form QA sets; Section B.2 ). Five automated isolation tests
( Section H.1 ) check that toggling one component does not
silently change another, including that two sessions with opposite
settings each keep their own configuration; this supports attributing
the interaction estimates in Section 5 to the components we
vary rather than to cross-stage leakage. A new component becomes a publishable comparison
in three steps ( Fig. 2 ): register with a decorator,
declare a factorial sweep in YAML, and run end-to-end to receive a
paired statistical test against the same surrounding stack that
produced every reported number. The complete study, factorial plus
138 non-factorial ablations plus the 5K–200K scaling sweep, cost
approximately $5,200 in cloud compute and 310 wall-clock hours
( Section A.7 ).

blocks.en:
Production RAG deployments operate against heterogeneous knowledge
bases where a single retriever must disambiguate biomedical,
financial, scientific, argumentative, and multi-hop queries from one
shared vector store. Per-benchmark evaluation (the
BEIR default; Thakur et al., 2021 ) under-tests this cross-domain
distractor pressure. We therefore unify our eight evaluation
benchmarks into one corpus: five BEIR sets cover retrieval (NFCorpus, Boteva et al., 2016 ; FiQA, Maia et al., 2018 ; SciFact, Wadden et al., 2020 ; ArguAna, Wachsmuth et al., 2018 ;
HotpotQA, Yang et al., 2018 ) and three QA sets cover generation
(SQuAD v2, Rajpurkar et al., 2018 ; MuSiQue, Trivedi et al., 2022 ), yielding 149 stratified queries
per configuration ( Sections B.2 , B.1 , 17 , 16 and 15 ). Each
configuration is evaluated on two tracks: retrieval (BEIR
qrels over 5,132 documents, 93 queries) and end-to-end
generation (the same corpus augmented with gold passages, 5,566
documents, 56 queries). Beyond the 167-run factorial, we
additionally ran 138 non-factorial ablation configurations across 24
targeted experiments spanning rerankers, embeddings, chunkers, query
augmentation, and the number of agentic verification iterations
( Appendix F ).
Together with the corpus-scaling sweep ( 5 5 K– 200 200 K), the study
records approximately 358,215 individual query evaluations,
including repeated RAGAS evaluation tasks for the same queries
( Section A.1 ).

blocks.en:
Most published RAG ablations tune one component at a time on a
single benchmark at ≤ 50 \leq 50 K corpus, and report the resulting gain
as a recommended configuration. We pre-declared ( van Miltenburg et al., 2021 ; Forde & Paganini, 2019 ) three hypotheses
that together test whether this methodology is sound, by asking
whether RAG pipelines can be designed compositionally: H1 tests additivity (the assumption behind isolated
single-component ablations), H2 tests profile
generality (the assumption that a single balanced recipe deploys
across targets), and H3 tests scale invariance (the
assumption that rankings measured on small corpora persist at larger
corpus scales). The full pre-registration (operational definitions,
statistical thresholds, exclusion criteria, post-hoc corrections) is
reproduced in Section A.2 . H1 Components do not necessarily combine additively. H1 tests whether two-way interactions among the eight experimental
dimensions explain at least 20 % 20\% of faithfulness variance. If they
do, gains measured in isolation cannot be assumed to persist when
components are combined. H2 A single RAG composition can span multiple deployment targets. RAG designs face a Pareto tradeoff: retrieval quality,
faithfulness, and response time cannot be maximized jointly,
so practitioners typically re-run configuration search per
deployment. H2 asks whether an intermediate RAG composition
sweeps a wider quality / latency / cost hypervolume than
adding more advanced components does, on a majority of
datasets, covering enough of the Pareto surface that one
published recipe serves multiple targets. Rejecting H2 means
each deployment must hand-tune its own operating point
(formalism and correction: Section A.2 ). H3 Composition rankings shift with corpus scale. Most RAG ablations in the literature run at 5K to 50K
documents, but production deployments often serve corpora
an order of magnitude larger. H3 asks whether the ranking of
RAG compositions at 5K matches their ranking at 200K on the
same corpus; if it does not, small-corpus rankings do not
transfer across scale, and design decisions measured at one
scale must be revalidated at the target scale. Confirming
H3 means small-corpus benchmarks are methodologically suspect
as scale-invariant selectors of RAG designs; rejecting it
validates them as predictive across the scales tested
(per-composition log-linear fits, slope-range threshold,
bootstrap CIs, and Kendall’s τ \tau rank-flip test in Section A.2 ).

blocks.en: 5 Results
blocks.zh: 5 结果

blocks.en:
Across the factorial and targeted tests, some techniques reinforce
one another, some add roughly as expected, and others overlap or
interfere ( Fig. 3 ). Thus, improvements measured by changing
one pipeline stage at a time do not reliably add up in a complete RAG
pipeline. We quantify this by comparing the gain predicted from
separately measured improvements with the gain the combined pipeline
actually delivers. This needs only the configurations the study already
runs, whereas estimating all 28 28 pairwise interactions directly requires 232 232 parameters, more than a design of this size can support
( Section D.3 ). The three largest separately measured retrieval gains, from
cross-encoder reranking, disabling MMR, and document-awareness
prefixes, predict a + 46.6 % +46.6\% lift over the default_standard baseline
(NDCG@10 = 0.412 =0.412 ; Table 32 ). On this same split a BM25-only
retriever scores 0.403 0.403 and a recommended off-the-shelf dense encoder 0.436 0.436 ( Table 60 ), so this is a realistic starting
point, not a weak one. The balanced pipeline,
which combines these techniques, realizes only + 17.2 % +17.2\% , a 63 % 63\% shortfall relative to the three-technique prediction. Including all
five separately positive retrieval techniques raises the shortfall to 72 % 72\% ( Fig. 9 ); across 17 tested combinations, it
ranges from 7 % 7\% to 72 % 72\% , with a median of 41 % 41\% ( Sections D.14 and D.12 ). The ablations suggest partial
functional overlap: reranking already provides some of the filtering
benefit obtained by disabling MMR, leaving less room for the two
techniques to help when combined. The target metric matters as well:
embedding, enrichment, and reranking dominate the retrieval-quality
metric, whereas query augmentation and agentic gating dominate the
answer-faithfulness metric, which measures whether generated claims
are supported by the retrieved context. Across matched pipeline
configurations, the two metrics are essentially unrelated
( Fig. 7 ; pooled Pearson r = − 0.01 r=-0.01 , p = 0.91 p=0.91 ): 5 % 5\% of configurations combine high faithfulness with low retrieval
quality, and 6 % 6\% show high retrieval quality with low faithfulness.
The same near-zero relationship appears when each benchmark is
examined separately, removing the concern that the near-zero
correlation is caused by pooling benchmarks ( Section D.2 ).
This indicates that RAG pipeline selection must evaluate both metrics:
selecting a pipeline based only on the retrieval metric can yield strong
retrieval but weakly grounded answers, while selecting one based only on
the faithfulness metric can hide poor retrieval.

survive both Bonferroni and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction:
Embedding × \times Enrichment ( η 2 = 0.102 \eta^{2}=0.102 ) and
Embedding × \times Reranking ( η 2 = 0.110 \eta^{2}=0.110 ). Both survivors
involve the embedding model. We attribute Embedding × \times Enrichment
to representation capacity: stronger embedders can encode added
context without diluting the original passage. We attribute
Embedding × \times Reranking to candidate-set quality: rerankers
have less room to help when the initial embedding already retrieves
strong candidates ( Sections J.3.1 and J.3.2 ). MMR reduces NDCG@10 by 3.6 % 3.6\% relative
on average, opposite its usual benefit on broad, heterogeneous corpora
( Table 44 ). We hypothesize that on focused-domain corpora
passages with high lexical and semantic overlap are often the same
supporting evidence, so MMR’s diversity penalty demotes them in favor
of topically distant ones (see Sections D.12 and D.13 ).

blocks.en:
Faithfulness shows a different additivity pattern. A
one-factor-at-a-time estimate based on BGE-large embeddings,
hierarchical chunking, hybrid-BM25 retrieval, and Speculative-RAG
gating predicts a + 28 % +28\% gain over a reference configuration, while
the best full RAG pipeline improves by + 32 % +32\% over the same reference.
This suggests that some faithfulness gains may combine approximately
as measured. We hypothesize that this occurs when techniques act at
complementary pipeline stages and duplicate less of one another’s function
( Table 47 ). Full pairwise results are
in Table 33 .

H1 (additivity): gains measured one component at a time do not carry over when components are combined, and how much is lost depends on the metric. Combining components loses most of the predicted retrieval gain and almost
none of the predicted faithfulness gain. The three strongest
single-component retrieval improvements predict + 47 % +47\% NDCG@10 and the
pipeline containing all three realizes + 17 % +17\% ; the same exercise on
faithfulness predicts + 28 % +28\% and realizes + 32 % +32\% ( Section D.14 ). Our pre-declared test of H1 was not met, and that outcome fits the same
split. It asked whether pairwise interactions explain at least 20 % 20\% of
the variance in faithfulness, the metric on which components combine
nearly additively, and they do not ( Section D.3 ). A
focused follow-up, pre-specified before it ran, confirms that the
interaction the broad analysis flagged is real ( p = 0.007 p=0.007 ) but far below
that bar ( Sections D.9 and D.10 ). New
components should therefore be evaluated inside representative complete
pipelines, on both metrics.

We extend the 5,132-document base corpus with scaling increments
(15K/25K/50K/100K/200K) under the same proportional sampling
protocol, with no distractor overlapping any evaluation query’s
relevant set. For 25K–200K, repeated seeded executions resample
retrieval and generation stochasticity but not corpus composition;
distractors are sampled from the same five BEIR source domains
as the base corpus (full protocol in Section B.3 ). NDCG@10 across six corpus sizes
separates into two regimes ( Fig. 4(a) ): speed and standard degrade log-linearly, while balanced and max-reliable are approximately flat.
The regimes cross between 15K and 25K. standard leads at
the small sizes (5K, 15K); balanced leads from 25K onward.
At 200K, balanced exceeds standard by 13.7 % 13.7\% relative ( p = 0.003 p=0.003 ; full per-size table in Section E.1 ).

We attribute the flatter retrieval-NDCG degradation at scale of balanced to several retrieval-stage additions relative to standard : broader chunk retention, hierarchical document
partitioning, and post-retrieval merging (full list in Section I.1 ). Together, these sustain a denser,

document-awareness prefixes that balanced additionally enables
act post-retrieval and pre-generation respectively; they primarily
support faithfulness rather than the NDCG@10 gap
( Section D.12 ; examples in document awareness and the 50K crossover ). speed degrades
fastest, which we hypothesize reflects MiniLM-L6’s limited
discriminative capacity (384-dim) operating without the lexical
anchoring that BM25 would provide under hybrid retrieval, see example and Table 23 for results.

Despite NDCG@10 falling as gold passages dilute among distractors,
faithfulness does not decline with corpus scale. All three
quality-focused profiles peak around 50K, dip at 100K, and recover
from 100K to 200K

We hypothesize that a larger corpus expands information coverage,
so that even when the gold document falls below the top- k k , other
documents contain overlapping or paraphrased content sufficient to
ground a faithful answer; the 100K → \to 200K recovery across all
three profiles is consistent with this mechanism. Full per-profile
slopes and 1M projections in Tables 23 , 22 , 11 and 49 ;
latency scaling at each corpus size in Fig. 10 .

At the fixed 30 30 s response-time reference, standard has the highest joint hypervolume ( 0.523 0.523 ). Within
the agentic pair, balanced improves NDCG@10 by 4.5 % 4.5\% and

generation favors response time, while iterative verification favors
faithfulness. Thus, additional components can improve one metric
without improving the complete RAG pipeline, so all three metrics
should be evaluated jointly.

H2 (single-composition generality): no complete RAG profile is best on every metric. At the fixed 30 30 s reference, standard achieves the

Thus, the best configuration depends on the target metrics, and
adding components does not guarantee a better pipeline.

blocks.en:
A sweep of 138 configurations across 24 targeted experiments yields
several practical findings ( Appendix F ). Across
20 configurations, chunker choice spans 0.126 0.126 NDCG@10, a 36 % 36\% relative difference larger than most factorial main effects
( Table 55 ). Thus, preprocessing choices
should also be tested within the complete pipeline. The 2019 MS-MARCO
MiniLM-L6 cross-encoder ( Nogueira & Cho, 2019 ) ranks above all
four recent rerankers tested ( Table 51 ); we
speculate that its training aligns especially well with our focused
domains. Matryoshka truncation of BGE-M3 to 768
dimensions ( Kusupati et al., 2022 ) reduces vector storage
and search cost by 25 % 25\% while improving NDCG@10 by 2.3 % 2.3\% ( Table 52 ). We attribute the gain to the
Matryoshka training objective, which concentrates useful signal in
leading dimensions; encoder cost is unchanged because the full vector
is computed first. On generation, faithfulness
is highest with hallucination and answer-quality gates disabled:
gate-triggered refinement can remove supporting evidence, including 14
of 15 chunks in one multi-hop example
( Table 54 ). HyDE raises NDCG@10 by 3.1 % 3.1\% but doubles first-hop latency, reducing the latency-adjusted
gain to 0.9 % 0.9\% , so its value depends on the latency budget
( Section I.2 ).

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We study how modern RAG techniques compose across pipeline stages,
metrics, and corpus scales using lasagna , a stage-isolated
framework, and 450 450 configurations across eight benchmarks from 5K
to 200K documents. Gains measured one component at a time do not
necessarily persist in complete pipelines; retrieval quality and
answer faithfulness favor different choices; and the best composition
changes with corpus scale. New techniques should be tested in
representative complete pipelines, on both metrics, and at the
intended scale. We release lasagna to make such studies
practical and reproducible, and to establish compositional
evaluation as the reporting standard for new RAG techniques rather
than the isolated single-component ablations common today.

我们研究现代RAG技术如何跨越管道阶段构成,
使用相位同位素的平面尺度
5K的8个基准的450个组合

必须在整个管道中坚持;检索质量和
忠贞的回答是倾向于不同的选择,而最佳的构成
随体积变化。 新技术应在
具有代表性的完整管道,在两个度量衡上和在
计划规模。 我们放出面条来做这种研究
具有实用性和可复制性,并确定构成
将评价作为新的RAG技术的报告标准
而不是今天常见的孤立的单一成分。

blocks.en: Ethics statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en:
LASAGNA is an evaluation framework operating over publicly released
retrieval benchmarks; no human subjects, personal data, or private
corpora were used. LLM API calls totalled approximately $5,200 and
310 wall-clock hours ( Section A.7 ); we report per-configuration
cost and latency to enable reproducibility on constrained budgets.
Because the framework lowers the cost of composing RAG pipelines,
users deploying it in domain applications requiring corpus-specific
validation should re-validate our profile candidates on their own
corpus before deployment. Our headline profile comparisons rest on
one constructed English multi-domain test bed with ≤ 93 \leq 93 retrieval and ≤ 200 \leq 200 generation queries per experiment, so the
profiles are best interpreted as candidates for further validation,
not prescriptions.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Our evaluation uses one constructed English multi-domain test bed
( ≤ 93 \leq 93 retrieval queries, ≤ 200 \leq 200 generation queries per
experiment) and does not test: multilingual corpora, real
enterprise or private data, open-weight generators (all headline
results use proprietary APIs; see Reproducibility Statement), or
cross-organizational large corpora. Faithfulness is now measured under
two generator models rather than one ( Section F.9 ), which
is a sensitivity check on generator choice and not a sweep: both models
are proprietary, and the ordering of the two closest profiles is not
stable across them. Findings should be interpreted
as case-study evidence for the methodological framework, and
derived profiles as candidates for further validation rather than
prescriptions for high-stakes deployments. The benchmarks are
concentrated in five focused domains (biomedical, financial,
scientific, argumentative, and multi-hop QA over Wikipedia), and
the corpus-scaling protocol injects controlled distractors drawn
from those same five domains. On the evaluation side, our cross-judge
(LLM and humans) agreement supports profile rankings across
LLM judges, but absolute faithfulness scores still live in a single
judge’s calibration. The confirmatory faithfulness experiment
(E1, Section D.10 ) meets its pre-registered
three-seed replication ( n runs = 3 n_{\text{runs}}=3 ) but uses 43 43 unique
queries rather than the pre-registered 200 200 , due to GPT-5.1
rate-limit budget cuts ( Appendix A ); magnitude
estimates should be read under this reduced query sampling. A
controlled length-variant rerun ( Section C.3 ) further
shows that raw faithfulness is partly length-driven, and that the
concise-over-verbose gap reverses under length control; we therefore
report both raw and length-residualized faithfulness for any
cross-regime claim. The within-regime results in the main tables are
unaffected because they hold prompt length constant. Our component
inventory is also a January-2026 snapshot of a literature that ships
new techniques actively. Scaling degradations should be read as an
upper bound: a formal n = 100 n{=}100 distractor-relevance audit
( Section B.3.5 ) finds a 0 % 0\% false-negative rate and a 9 % 9\% partial-relevance rate, so the H3 rank-flip is robust to
distractor mis-labeling but true degradation is likely smaller than
reported.

blocks.en: A.2.1 Motivation and Rationale
blocks.zh: A.2.1 动机和理由

blocks.en:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation ( Lewis et al., 2020 ) has become the
dominant paradigm for grounding large language models in external
knowledge. A rich toolkit of individually validated
techniques, dense retrieval, hybrid sparse–dense fusion, cross-encoder
reranking, HyDE ( Gao et al., 2023a ) , CRAG ( Yan et al., 2024 ) ,
Self-RAG ( Asai et al., 2024 ) , is available to practitioners, yet
each technique is evaluated in isolation against a simple baseline.
Practitioners who combine several techniques simultaneously have no
empirical basis for predicting whether their gains add, cancel, or
amplify.

blocks.en:
This is not merely a reporting gap. Wang et al. (2024) observe that end-to-end RAG performance
depends on coordinated pipeline design rather than any single component; Chen et al. (2026) confirm the presence of interaction effects by
showing that jointly optimized RAG components outperform independently
tuned ones. Yet neither work measures the sign, magnitude, or
domain-dependence of these interactions under controlled factorial
conditions, precisely the question a practitioner faces when choosing a
configuration for production.

blocks.en: A.2.2 Pre-Registered Hypotheses
blocks.zh: A.2.2 预先登记的假设

blocks.en:
We pre-register three hypotheses that together ask whether RAG
pipelines can be designed compositionally. H1 asks the structural question: do the eight pipeline components combine
additively, or do they interact non-trivially? If they interact, the
implicit assumption behind every single-component ablation in the
literature fails. H2 asks the design question:
assuming components do interact, can a single fixed configuration
still serve practitioners across the (faithfulness, latency, cost)
tradeoff space, or must each deployment hand-tune for its own
operating point? H3 asks the scaling question: do the
answers to H1 and H2 survive a 40 × 40\times scale-up of the corpus, or
are small-corpus best practices misleading at production scale?

practice.

This pre-registration is published before experimental data collection
to establish hypothesis commitment and invite community input.
We welcome feedback on: 1. additional hypotheses worth testing within this factorial
framework, 2. model selection for generation and evaluation
(Section A.2.3 ), 3. benchmark composition and domain coverage, 4. statistical methodology and effect-size thresholds. All community-suggested modifications adopted before experiments begin
will be documented as amendments; post-experiment suggestions will be
addressed as exploratory analyses in the companion paper.

blocks.en:
Fedorov coordinate exchange ( Fedorov et al., 1972 ; Atkinson et al., 2007 ) is a greedy row-exchange algorithm that starts from a random 242-row
subset of the 30,720-row full-factorial candidate set and iteratively
swaps one in-design row for the candidate row that most increases the
D-criterion ϕ D ​ ( 𝐗 ) = det ( 𝐗 ⊤ ​ 𝐗 ) , \phi_{D}(\mathbf{X})=\det(\mathbf{X}^{\top}\mathbf{X}), (1) terminating when no single-row swap raises the determinant. The model
matrix 𝐗 \mathbf{X} is 242 × 232 242\times 232 and encodes one intercept, 22
main-effect contrasts, and 209 two-way interaction contrasts under effect coding (factor levels mapped to ± 1 \pm 1 rather than the 0 / 1 0/1 of dummy coding, so main effects are orthogonal to the intercept).
A custom Python implementation ( experiments/design/generate_design_matrix.py , available from the authors on request) reproduces the
matrix bit-identically at seed = 42 =42 .

blocks.en:
No graph configuration improves over the baseline, and NDCG@10 decreases
monotonically as graph-hop depth grows (1-hop → \to 3-hop, − 0.011 -0.011 ).
One plausible explanation, consistent with the retrieval–faithfulness
asymmetry observed in the full factorial ( Section 5 ), is
that graph-derived structural context may aid answer grounding while
diluting passage-level similarity signals on these domain-focused
corpora, where lexical and semantic retrieval already locate the gold
evidence. We did not evaluate the generation-track faithfulness effect,
so this is a hypothesis rather than a claim. Given the lack of NDCG@10
signal and the ∼ {\sim} 14-hour per-combo ingestion cost, we excluded
GraphRAG from the 167-run factorial ( Table 10 , D3) and the
scaling runs ( Section 5 ).

blocks.en:
Table 12: Pre-registration reconciliation. “Confirmatory” items retain
their original inferential status; “Exploratory” items are presented
without confirmatory p p -values.

The original 242-config factorial assumed access to a dedicated GPU cluster
and a corpus pipeline capable of ingesting up to 1M documents. During
execution, two constraints materialized: (1) all LLM inference was routed
through an enterprise API gateway to GPT-5.1, which imposed rate
limits that made concurrent large-scale runs infeasible, and (2) our Milvus Lite
instance required fresh database resets between embedding-model groups to
avoid dimension-mismatch errors. We executed 167 of 242 planned
configurations (69%) across all 8 dimensions, 4 embedding models, 4
chunking strategies, 3 of 4 enrichment levels (GraphRAG excluded due
to entity-extraction cost of ∼ {\sim} 14 hours per ingestion combo), 3
retrieval modes, 5 query augmentation strategies, 4 reranking modes, 2
compression settings, and 4 agentic gate levels. The 167-configuration
subset preserves all 22 main effects and enables estimation of all 28
two-way interactions via ANOVA, though with reduced power for the
missing GraphRAG enrichment level. Twelve additional configurations
failed due to Milvus Lite query-limit errors and are excluded.

(df sum 172 + 226 > n − 1 = 338 172{+}226{>}n{-}1{=}338 , arithmetically impossible) and
inflated the reported η 2 \eta^{2} from 0.428 0.428 to 0.546 0.546 .

blocks.en: Deviations from the Preregistration

blocks.en:
This section consolidates every deviation between the pre-registered
protocol and the executed study. Each
row of Table 12 above enumerates a scientific
deviation; the list below adds executional and reporting deviations
that are not obvious from that table.
blocks.zh:
本节汇总了预先登记的每个偏差
协议和已执行的研究。 每个
以上表12一行列出了科学
偏差; 以下列表添加执行偏差和报告偏差
这从桌子上看并不明显。

blocks.en:
• Configuration count : 242 planned → \rightarrow 167
factorial configurations executed (69% of the design), plus 138
non-factorial ablation configurations; shortfall driven by rate
limits on the enterprise API gateway and Milvus Lite
dimension-mismatch resets between embedding-model groups. • Enrichment dimension (D3) reduction : 4 planned
levels → \rightarrow 3 executed. The graphrag level was
dropped after an isolated ablation showed no NDCG@10 gain
against the entity-extraction cost ( ∼ \sim 14 hours per ingestion
combo); this is a scientific deviation not previously
surfaced in Table 12 . • Timeouts : 12 additional configurations were
attempted and timed out on Milvus Lite query limits; excluded
from all analyses. • Per-configuration query count : preregistered budget
of 2,300 queries per configuration → \rightarrow executed 93
queries per retrieval configuration and 43 43 generation / 56 56 retrieval queries per SOTA-profile E2E configuration.
The reduction is a straight
budget cut driven by GPT-5.1 rate limits; power calculations
for the H1 factorial were re-run at the reduced counts and are
reported in Section D.3 . • Benchmark substitution : preregistered MS MARCO and
CUAD were replaced with TriviaQA and BEIR/FiQA. MS MARCO was
dropped because its passage license conflicts with our
reproducibility artifact policy; CUAD was replaced with FiQA
(which supplies a comparable domain-specific IR task) to keep
coverage of financial/regulatory text without the CUAD license
constraint. • H2 corpus scope : the pre-registered H2 Pareto
protocol specified a multi-benchmark hypervolume comparison; the
executed H2 headline reports a joint NDCG@10, faithfulness, and
response-time comparison on one SQuAD v2 / MuSiQue / HotpotQA
mixture ( 43 43 generation / 56 56 retrieval queries per seed, three
seeded runs).
This mixture emerged as the practical H2 test after the
MS MARCO / CUAD substitution above eliminated the two
pre-registered benchmarks that would have anchored the
multi-benchmark comparison. The executed comparison therefore does
not confirm the pre-registered cross-benchmark claim; the original
multi-benchmark
grid is fully specified in Section D.7 but was not
executed. A separate
post-hoc replication of the H2 pattern on the same three benchmark
families at 100K and 200K is reported descriptively in Section D.8 ; it is supplementary and
does not substitute for the pre-registered multi-benchmark grid. The balanced profile should therefore be read as a
candidate starting point pending validation on the target corpus,
exactly as the H2 verdict box states. • Scaling-fit form : preregistered power-law fit a ⋅ N b a\cdot N^{b} → \rightarrow executed log-linear fit a ⋅ log 10 ⁡ ( N ) + b a\cdot\log_{10}(N)+b (see the “Deviation from the
pre-registered fit form” paragraph in Section B.3.9 ). • H1 test statistic : the pre-registered joint
232-parameter 28-two-way F F -test is unidentifiable on
the 113-configuration data (232 parameters vs. 339 rows,
rank-deficient Plackett-Burman × \times screener cells). We
executed the pre-registered per-pair Bonferroni correction
( α / 28 \alpha/28 ) instead and added an adequately-powered
focused-confirmatory experiment E1 (see Section D.9 )
post-hoc as a replacement for the joint test. • H1 decision-rule interpretation
(variance-floor vs. significance-floor) : the
pre-registration’s rejection rule is stated as
“interaction terms contribute < < 5% of variance → \rightarrow reject H1 / additivity holds within tolerance,” which is a variance threshold. The variance and significance criteria
yield different formal readings. Under the pre-registration’s
variance rule, the executed η 2 = 0.033 \eta^{2}=0.033 (E1) and η 2 = 0.040 \eta^{2}=0.040 (per-sample joint) both sit on the additivity-holds side of the 5% floor. Under the parallel
significance criterion ( p < 0.05 p<0.05 ), strict-zero additivity is
rejected, but the effect sizes are small. Both readings appear in
the reconciliation table and H1 verdict box and support the same
practical conclusion (main effects dominate; cell-level
residuals are non-trivial but small in aggregate). • Distractor-relevance audit : performed post-hoc
( n = 100 n{=}100 LLM-audited pairs; see Section B.3.5 ):
false-negative rate 0.0 % 0.0\% (95% CI [ 0.0 % , 0.0 % ] [0.0\%,0.0\%] ), any-signal
rate 9.0 % 9.0\% (all partial, biomedical-concentrated). Given FN < 5 % \text{FN}{<}5\% , the audit supports treating the H3 rank-flip
as robust on the audited splits and the reported scaling
degradations as an upper bound (see
the “Distractor-relevance caveat” paragraph in Section 5 ). • Corpus fingerprints : SHA-256 fingerprints for the
100K/200K corpus files are unavailable
( Section B.3.4 ); the draw is reproducible from the seed-42 sampling script (available from the authors on request), so reconstruction relies on the
recipe rather than content-addressed corpus files.

blocks.en: B.1 Evaluation Dataset Design
blocks.zh: B.1 评价数据集设计

blocks.en:
We designed a three-track evaluation protocol that separates retrieval quality
measurement from generation quality measurement and hallucination resistance
testing. Each track uses a purpose-built corpus to ensure that the measured
outcome reflects the intended evaluation dimension.
blocks.zh:
我们设计了三轨评估协议 将检索质量分开
从生成质量测量和幻觉阻力中测量
测试。 每个轨道都使用专门设计的装置,以确保测量到的
结果反映了预期的评价方面。

blocks.en:
Each configuration is evaluated on 149 non-overlapping queries: 93 for
retrieval (stratified across 5 BEIR domains) and 56 for generation
(stratified across 3 QA benchmarks). These representative subsets were
drawn via stratified random sampling from the full benchmark pools
(which collectively contain thousands of queries) to balance domain
coverage and difficulty distribution against the ∼ \sim $4,700
compute budget required for factorial-scale evaluation (167
configurations × \times 149 queries = 24,883 =24{,}883 retrieval evaluations
plus 6,832 generation evaluations). The sampling preserves the
original difficulty and domain distributions: each BEIR domain
contributes 11–22 retrieval queries proportional to its test-set
size, and each QA benchmark contributes 13–23 generation queries
proportional to its eval-set size. While larger query sets would
reduce per-configuration variance, the factorial design compensates
by aggregating signal across 167 independent configurations,
yielding 71,643 total evaluations, sufficient for main-effect
and targeted-interaction testing at 80% power for η 2 ≥ 0.03 \eta^{2}\geq 0.03 ( Section 5 ).

blocks.en:
We drew documents from five BEIR domain subsets: nfcorpus , fiqa , scifact , arguana , and hotpotqa .
These subsets span biomedical, financial, scientific, argumentative, and
multi-hop reasoning domains, providing heterogeneous retrieval challenges.
blocks.zh:
我们从五个BEIR域分集中绘制出文件:nfcorpus、fiqa、scifact、arguana、和热点qa。
这些子集涵盖生物医学、金融、科学、论证和
多跳推理域,提供多样的检索挑战.

blocks.en:
For each benchmark we sampled 500 distractor documents from held-out BEIR
collections that do not overlap with the benchmark’s relevance judgments.
Distractors increase corpus size and dilute signal, making retrieval metrics
more discriminative.
blocks.zh:
我们为每个基准抽取了500份来自BEIR的分散注意力文件
与基准相关判断不相重叠的集合。
干扰器增加体积并稀释信号,使检索量度
更具有歧视性。

blocks.en:
For the end-to-end generation track (Track 2), we extracted context passages
from each QA sample by splitting on double newlines ( \n\n ). Each
extracted passage was assigned a document identifier of the form gold:{benchmark}:{sample_id}:{passage_idx} and ingested
alongside the base corpus. With 500 distractors per benchmark, gold passages
represent roughly 8% of the Track 2 corpus; this ratio is substantially lower
than the 84% we observed in early pilots that used only 100 distractors,
yielding a more realistic retrieval challenge.

对于端到端生成轨道(轨道2),我们提取了上下文段落
通过在双新线上分拆(\n\n)从每个QA样本中取出. 每个
提取的段落被指派为表单金的文档标识符 : {基准}: { sample_id}: { passage_idx} 并被摄取
与基质。 每个基准有500个分心者,黄金通道

比早期飞行员只使用100个分心器的 84%
产生更现实的检索挑战。

blocks.en:
We partitioned all queries into 60/20/20 train/eval/test splits, stratified by
source benchmark, so that each split contains a proportional representation of
every domain. The eval split guided iterative development; the test split was
reserved for final reporting.

每一个领域。 eval分解引导迭代开发;测试分解为:

blocks.en: B.1.3 Design Rationale
blocks.zh: B.1.3 设计理由

blocks.en: We separate the three tracks for the following reasons:
blocks.zh: 我们分离这三条轨道的原因如下:

blocks.en:
1. Retrieval track. Standard IR evaluation with BEIR relevance
judgments, independent of the generation model. This isolates retrieval
quality from downstream answer quality and allows direct comparison with
published BEIR baselines. 2. E2E generation track. Tests the full pipeline, including
answer generation. Gold passages are present in the corpus so that the
retriever can find them; failure to produce a correct answer
therefore reflects pipeline limitations rather than corpus gaps. 3. Hallucination track. Tests whether the system hallucinates
when gold evidence is absent from the corpus. A faithful system should

blocks.en: B.1.5 Ingestion Signature and Corpus Reuse
blocks.zh: B.1.5 摄入签字和重新使用

blocks.en:
To avoid redundant re-ingestion across experiments that differ only in
query-time configuration, we key corpus reuse on a hash of the ingestion
parameters: (corpus_id, corpus_fingerprint, embedding_model,
embedding_dim, chunking_params) . Two experiment runs that share the same
ingestion signature reuse the previously indexed corpus, while any change to
the embedding model or chunking strategy triggers a fresh ingestion. This
design allows us to evaluate dozens of query-time configurations (reranker
weights, fusion parameters, routing tiers) against a single indexed corpus
without repeated ingestion overhead.
blocks.zh:
避免在实验中重复重新摄入,这些实验仅与
查询时间配置, 我们在摄取的散列上重用密钥体
参数:(公司、单位、指印、嵌入_模型、
嵌入_dim, 块_参数) 。 两次实验都一样
摄取签名重用先前索引的元件,而任何更改均改为
嵌入模型或块化策略引发了新的摄入。 这个
设计允许我们评价数十个查询时间配置( 重排)
加权、聚变参数、路由级)与单一指数化体相对
而不重复摄入额。

blocks.en: B.3.3 Scaling Protocol
blocks.zh: B.3.3 扩大议定书

blocks.en:
Each profile × \times size combination is run with a freshly
initialized vector database to prevent index contamination from
prior runs. The protocol for each run is: 1. Delete the existing vector database file. 2. Swap the corpus file with the scaled version (base + relevant
increments). 3. Ingest all documents and build the BM25 fallback index. 4. Run all evaluation queries (93 retrieval or 56 E2E generation). 5. Compute metrics (NDCG@10, Faithfulness via RAGAS, Exact Match). 6. Restore the original corpus file. All results are single-run point estimates. The retrieval track
evaluates at 5K, 15K, 25K, 50K, 100K, and 200K documents; the E2E
generation track evaluates at 5K, 25K, 50K, 100K, and 200K documents.
blocks.zh:
每个 profile ×\times 大小组合以新程序运行
初始化矢量数据库,防止指数污染
先前运行。 每次运行的协议是: 1. 删除现有的矢量数据库文件. 2. 用缩放的版本(基数+相关)来交换诉讼案卷

blocks.en:
Two mechanisms besides information coverage may contribute to the
observed faithfulness improvements at scale. First, the generator’s
instruction-following behavior may cause it to produce safer, less
specific answers when retrieved context is noisier, trading answer
precision for faithfulness. Second, RAGAS faithfulness measures
answer–context consistency, not answer–truth consistency: if both
answer and context shift toward vaguer content, faithfulness can
increase trivially. Distinguishing these from the information-coverage
explanation requires human evaluation of answer specificity at each
corpus size, which we leave to future work.

blocks.en: C.1 Evaluation Metrics

blocks.en:
This appendix provides formal definitions for every evaluation metric
exposed by lasagna ’s evaluation SDK, grouped into retrieval
metrics (computed before generation), end-to-end answer metrics, and
LLM-judged metrics. The main paper reports NDCG@10, MRR, Recall@100,
EM, Token F1, and RAGAS faithfulness; the remaining metrics defined
below (answer relevance, pairwise LLM-as-judge preference, MAP, and

blocks.en: C.1.4 Judge Bias and Mitigations
blocks.zh: C.1.4 法官比亚斯和减刑

blocks.en:
LLM judges exhibit well-documented biases that can distort
evaluation ( Zheng et al., 2023 ) . Our protocol mitigates three
of these biases, described below.
blocks.zh:
LLM法官表现出有据可查的可扭曲偏见
评估(郑等,2023). 我们的规矩减轻了三个
这些偏见,说明如下。

blocks.en:
LLM judges tend to prefer the answer presented first in the
prompt ( Zheng et al., 2023 ) . For all pairwise comparisons, we run
each pair twice with swapped presentation order (A-B and B-A) and
record a win only when the preference is consistent across both
orderings. Inconsistent pairs are counted as ties.

blocks.en:
Models may prefer outputs from the same model family. Because both
answer generation (GPT-5.1) and judging (GPT-5.1) use the same
model, self-preference bias is a concern. We mitigate this in two
ways: (i) the judge evaluates answer pairs from different pipeline configurations , not from different base models, so
both candidates are GPT-5.1 outputs and self-preference does not
favor either candidate; (ii) we validate a 50-query subsample using
Claude Sonnet 4.5 as an alternative judge to measure inter-judge agreement.
We ran 80 matched samples (40 per configuration) through both judges.
Kendall’s τ b = 0.38 \tau_{b}=0.38 ( p < 0.001 p<0.001 ), Spearman ρ = 0.42 \rho=0.42 ( p < 0.001 p<0.001 ), and 66% of per-sample faithfulness scores agree within
0.1 absolute points. GPT-5.1 assigns slightly higher mean faithfulness
(0.879 vs. 0.860 for Claude Sonnet 4.5). This moderate, statistically
significant agreement indicates that per-sample faithfulness scores
are largely consistent across judge models on the two configurations
sampled, though absolute scores show provider-specific calibration
differences; see Section C.5 for a separate pairwise-BTL
protocol study showing that fine-grained configuration-level rankings
are protocol-dependent while profile-tier separations are preserved.

blocks.en: C.3 Length-Controlled Faithfulness Rerun

blocks.en:
A natural concern is that faithfulness gains under our
concise-answer prompting may partly reflect brevity, shorter answers
make fewer atomic claims and thus fewer opportunities for the RAGAS
judge to flag a claim as unsupported, rather than genuinely superior
grounding. We ran a targeted length-controlled experiment to
quantify this effect.

法官将索赔标为无根据,而不是真正优越
着陆 我们进行了目标长度控制实验
量化这一效应。

blocks.en:
We drew a stratified sample of 50 questions across three benchmarks
(SQuAD v2: 22, MuSiQue: 18, HotpotQA: 10) and re-generated answers
under three prompt regimes derived from a common instruction skeleton
that varies only length guidance: (A) concise (“answer in one
short sentence”), (B) neutral (“answer based on the
context”), and (C) verbose (“answer in detail with supporting
facts”). Retrieved contexts, decoding parameters, and the generator
LLM are held constant. All 50 × 3 = 150 50\times 3=150 answer–context pairs
are re-scored under the canonical GPT-5.1 faithfulness judge. Raw data ( paper/data/length_controlled_faith.jsonl ) and the analysis script ( paper/scripts/m6_length_analysis.py ) are available from the authors on request.

blocks.en:
The paper validates the RAGAS/GPT-5.1 faithfulness metric with three independent judge-validation studies that should not be
conflated: 1. Human dyad study (this appendix, n = 50 n=50 ): two human
annotators vs. RAGAS on 50 QA triples, yielding Pearson r = 0.83 r=0.83 against RAGAS and r = 0.96 r=0.96 between annotators; Cohen’s κ \kappa at the 0.5 midpoint = 0.92 =0.92 . 2. Cross-LLM study ( Section C.1.4 , n = 80 n=80 ): 40
matched configuration answers per profile scored by GPT-5.1 and Claude Sonnet 4.5, yielding Kendall’s τ b = 0.38 \tau_{b}=0.38 with 66% pairwise agreement within ± 0.10 \pm 0.10 . 3. Pairwise Bradley–Terry study
( Section C.5 , n = 123 n{=}123 pairs, 246 246 judgments): two independent LLM annotators fit a BTL posterior over 12
D5 × \times D8 configurations, yielding Cohen’s κ = 0.79 \kappa=0.79 (substantial inter-annotator agreement) and a Spearman ρ = − 0.36 \rho=-0.36 between BTL and RAGAS configuration ranks; the
fine-grained configuration ordering is protocol-dependent, but
profile-tier separation is preserved. These three studies use disjoint samples and answer different
questions (per-answer human calibration, cross-model robustness, and
pairwise configuration-ranking) and are therefore not pooled. Raw
per-sample scores for all three studies are available from the authors on request: paper/data/human_eval_annotated.json (human dyad), paper/data/judge_cross_validation_80.json (cross-LLM), and paper/data/human_eval_btl_posteriors.json (with per-item pairwise annotations in paper/data/human_eval_pairwise_btl_items_A1.csv and paper/data/human_eval_pairwise_btl_items_A2.csv ).

The human validation ( n = 50 n{=}50 examples across SQuAD v2, MuSiQue and

This sample is UNDER-POWERED to validate configuration-ranking-level
correlation across the 122 pipeline configurations in the faithfulness
factorial: at n = 50 n{=}50 the standard error on a Pearson correlation is ≈ 0.14 \approx 0.14 and the sample provides on average 50 / 122 ≈ 0.4 50/122\approx 0.4 observations per configuration, insufficient to
certify a Kendall’s- τ b \tau_{b} between per-configuration human means and
per-configuration RAGAS means. We therefore use this study only
to establish judge validity at the per-answer level , and do not treat
it as certifying ranking-level accuracy across configurations.
The two cross-LLM sensitivity studies described elsewhere
( Section C.1.4 n = 80 n{=}80 ; Section F.8 n = 220 n{=}220 ) supplement this human study, but do not substitute for it;
they measure robustness across judge models rather than validity
against human judgement, and remain LLM-scored throughout.
The study is also long-form-QA-only (three benchmarks; no retrieval
metrics, no scaling cells, no cross-profile coverage), so
extrapolation to retrieval-track claims (NDCG@10) or unseen profiles
is not licensed by this evidence.

blocks.en:
To validate the LLM-judged faithfulness metric, two domain experts
with RAG evaluation experience independently annotated 50
question–answer–context triples sampled from the generation
evaluation set (17 SQuAD v2, 18 MuSiQue, 15 HotpotQA). Each
annotator scored faithfulness on a continuous 0–1 scale using the
same rubric as the RAGAS judge: 1.0 if every claim is supported by
the context, 0.0 if no claims are supported. Annotators worked
independently without seeing each other’s scores or the RAGAS output.

of 1 means that every factual claim in the answer is supported by the
context. A score of 0 means that none of the factual claims are
supported. Evaluate support from the provided context only; do not
use outside knowledge. Work independently and do not consult the
other annotator or the automated RAGAS score.

blocks.en:
The n = 50 n{=}50 human study of Section C.4 establishes judge
validity at the per-answer level but is under-powered to certify
configuration-ranking accuracy across the D5 × \times D8 factorial. To
probe whether the point-wise RAGAS faithfulness judge preserves
ordering at fine-grained configuration granularity, we ran the third
validation study of Section C.4 using a pairwise
Bradley–Terry (BTL) LLM annotation protocol on 123 blinded
configuration-pairs drawn from the
D5 × \times D8 grid. Pairs were biased toward small RAGAS deltas
(top- K K nearest per shared sample) to concentrate the study on the
sub-noise regime the point-wise judge is least confident about. The
RAGAS anchor scores against which the BTL posteriors are correlated
in Table 30 (Spearman ρ = − 0.364 \rho=-0.364 ; Pearson r = − 0.421 r=-0.421 ) are computed under the concise-regen prompt
regime ( Sections C.2 and 26 ), matching the
122-configuration faithfulness ANOVA ( Sections D.2 and 3 )
from which the D5 × \times D8 slice is drawn. Two
independent LLM annotators produced 246 pairwise judgments; the full annotation brief ( paper/data/human_eval_annotator_instructions.md ) and raw per-item annotations ( paper/data/human_eval_pairwise_btl_items_A1.csv and paper/data/human_eval_pairwise_btl_items_A2.csv ) are available from the authors on request.

raw significance but not the Holm-corrected family-wise threshold.
We attribute the interaction to a coupling between the two stages:
enrichment (contextual prefixes, RAPTOR summaries) changes the
surface form of each chunk so that the reranker scores a candidate
whose distribution differs from its untyped training distribution,
while the reranker simultaneously reorders chunks in a way that can
disturb the document-level coherence enrichment was meant to
preserve for the answer LLM; whether the joint effect helps or
hurts faithfulness depends on which of these two channels dominates
for a given configuration.

To verify that the sequential one-at-a-time ANOVA does not produce
spurious interactions, we fit a joint LASSO-penalized regression

is the strongest surviving interaction pair (4 terms selected,
total | β | = 0.074 |\beta|=0.074 ), confirming the sequential ANOVA finding.

different data; both survive within-family Holm adjustment.

blocks.en:
Section D.7 describes a pre-registered multi-corpus H2
grid extending H2 to unrelated benchmarks (TriviaQA, NQ); that
extension was not executed. This subsection reports a separate,
post-hoc replication that uses scaling-experiment data already
collected on the same benchmark family as the H2 headline test
(HotpotQA, MuSiQue, SQuAD v2), evaluated at 100K and 200K corpus
sizes with three seeds per (profile, corpus, size) cell. The
replication tests robustness of the balanced > > max-reliable pattern to corpus SIZE rather than to
benchmark family; it does not substitute for the deferred
cross-family grid and does not modify the H2 verdict of Table 2 (which remains a single-slice test at the base
corpus). Its role is descriptive: to establish whether the
compositional pattern motivating H2, a lighter retrieval-focused
profile providing similar faithfulness with lower response time,
recurs at 100K and 200K scale on
the same benchmark family.

Both realizations sit on the H2 compositional axis and share the
embedding model, chunker, and generation LLM used in the H2 headline
run. The balanced -tier realization uses hybrid retrieval
( α = 0.3 \alpha{=}0.3 ), top- k = 20 k{=}20 retrieval breadth, extractive context
compression at 0.5 0.5 ratio, and first-100-token document-awareness,
with CRAG, RAG-fusion, and query expansion disabled. Its mean
per-sample latency across the three benchmarks is 6.4 6.4 s at 100K
and 8.3 8.3 s at 200K. The max-reliable -tier realization
uses hybrid retrieval ( α = 0.5 \alpha{=}0.5 ), a neural reranker
( mxbai-rerank-large-v1 ), HyDE query expansion at three draft
documents, extractive compression, and first-100-token
document-awareness. Its mean per-sample latency is 69.3 69.3 s at 100K
and 134.3 134.3 s at 200K. Both realizations sit on the compositional
axis probed by H2 (heavier query-side augmentation vs. broader
retrieval with light post-processing); they are two operating points
on that axis and are not identical to the profile pair in Tables 2 and I.1 , which is why we report this as
pattern replication rather than direct replication of the headline
test. Specifically, the balanced -tier realization used
here differs from the balanced profile specified in Section I.1 in three ways (hybrid α = 0.3 \alpha{=}0.3 vs. 0.5 0.5 ,
HyDE disabled vs. three-variant, no neural reranker vs. mxbai-rerank-large-v1 ), and the max-reliable -tier
realization used here omits the agentic gate that Section I.1 enables for the headline max-reliable profile; per-sample latency comparisons below should therefore not be
read against the p95 numbers in Section I.1 .

This replication uses profile realizations that sit on the H2
compositional axis but are not identical to the pair in Table 2 . It is therefore not a direct replication of the
H2 headline test; the pre-registered multi-corpus comparison in Section D.7 remains unexecuted. The compositional
H2 pattern (a lighter retrieval-focused profile providing similar
faithfulness with lower response time than a heavier configuration)
recurs at two corpus scales on the same
SQuAD v2 / MuSiQue / HotpotQA benchmark family as the H2 headline.
Because faithfulness gaps are non-significant in both directions
and the latency advantage holds on every sample, we treat the
observation as descriptive corroboration of the H2 pattern rather
than a new significance claim.

The exploratory factorial identified Query Augmentation × \times Agentic Gate as

a focused confirmatory study: (i) the 232-parameter joint model is
under-identified against the executed 122 usable generation configurations; and
(ii) the same query set was applied across configurations, so hierarchical
inference at the query level was more appropriate than flat OLS.

blocks.en:
While the aggregate D5 × \times D8 interaction is small on the E1 grid,
cell-level departures from the additive main-effects prediction reveal
specific compositional patterns that isolated single-component
ablations cannot see. Table 42 lists the top
five antagonistic and top five synergistic cells ranked by | | residual | | ; ten of twenty cells deviate from the additive
prediction by ≥ 0.02 {\geq}0.02 faithfulness, evenly split (five
antagonistic, five synergistic), with residuals spanning [ − 0.050 , + 0.047 ] [-0.050,+0.047] . Two structural patterns are visible: (i) Query
Decomposition synergizes with the active agentic gates: its two
largest positive residuals are with CRAG ( + 0.039 +0.039 ) and
Speculative-RAG ( + 0.047 +0.047 ), but it antagonizes the no-gate condition
( − 0.050 -0.050 ), i.e. multi-part queries need an active verifier
downstream to pay off; (ii) Speculative-RAG antagonizes passive or
lightly-augmented queries (residuals of − 0.041 -0.041 with both raw
queries and Query Expansion) yet synergizes with structured
decomposition ( + 0.047 +0.047 ), i.e. its parallel draft-and-verify
mechanism is worth the latency only when the upstream query already
carries structure. Both patterns are invisible to single-factor
ablations: a practitioner who tunes D5 and D8 independently would
predict the additive main-effects surface and miss up to ± 5 \pm 5 -point cell-level swings against that prediction. This is the
compositional evidence that motivates factorial testbeds like lasagna even when the aggregate interaction term is small.
The seven cells whose D8 level lies in {CRAG, Self-RAG,
Speculative-RAG} were re-scored by the pairwise-BTL follow-up in Section C.5 , which on a subsample deliberately biased
toward small RAGAS deltas returned 79 % 79\% ties and Spearman ρ = − 0.36 \rho=-0.36 between BTL and RAGAS configuration ranks; those seven
cell-level directions should therefore be read as protocol-dependent
descriptive patterns rather than judge-invariant orderings. The
five D8 = = none cells of the 5 × 4 5{\times}4 grid, including
the Query-Decomposition × \times none residual of − 0.050 -0.050 named
above, sit outside the BTL sample and are not certified by BTL
either way. The within-agentic three-level D8 ordering
(Speculative-RAG > > Self-RAG > > CRAG) that BTL directly probes via
item (ii) of Section C.5 is protocol-robust; the
four-level D8 marginal that includes none ( Section D.2 ) is not independently corroborated by BTL
because the BTL sample contains no D8 = = none configurations.

blocks.en:
Prior to the full factorial ANOVA, we conducted six 2 × 2 2{\times}2 factorial probes on the TriviaQA eval split (76 queries) targeting
four key components: reranking, hybrid alpha, MMR, and HyDE.
The interaction is estimated via the difference-in-differences (DiD)
estimator: τ ^ int = ( y ¯ 11 − y ¯ 10 ) − ( y ¯ 01 − y ¯ 00 ) , \widehat{\tau}_{\text{int}}=\bigl(\bar{y}_{11}-\bar{y}_{10}\bigr)-\bigl(\bar{y}_{01}-\bar{y}_{00}\bigr), (12) where y ¯ i ​ j \bar{y}_{ij} is mean NDCG@10 for factor levels i , j i,j .
Confidence intervals are constructed from a paired bootstrap (10,000
resamples, query-level pairing) with bias-corrected and accelerated
(BCa) adjustment.

We tested the two strongest probes on the held-out BEIR test split
(96 queries across 5 domains). Reranking × \times MMR replicated

beneficial in that profile); a positive Δ \Delta NDCG indicates that removing
the feature helps (i.e., the feature is harmful in that profile).
This analysis is exploratory.

blocks.en: D.14 The Composition Penalty

This appendix visualizes the central finding of the paper: that
composing individually beneficial RAG components yields smaller
improvements than the sum of their independent effects.

blocks.en:
The waterfall in Fig. 9 illustrates why single-factor
ablations are misleading for RAG pipeline design. Each bar represents
the marginal gain of one component when evaluated in isolation against
the baseline. A practitioner who selects components based on these
independent deltas would expect a combined NDCG@10 of 0.667
( = 0.412 + 0.084 + 0.062 + 0.046 + 0.037 + 0.026 =0.412+0.084+0.062+0.046+0.037+0.026 ). The actual
composed result is 0.483, a shortfall of 0.184 ( 72 % 72\% of the expected
improvement is lost to interactions).

This penalty arises because several components partially duplicate
each other’s function. For example, both HyDE and cross-encoder
reranking improve query-passage alignment, and when both are active
the marginal gain of each is smaller than when either operates alone.
Similarly, disabling MMR removes a diversity penalty that the reranker
already subsumes, so the independent gain from disabling MMR overlaps
with the gain from adding a reranker.

The measured balanced – standard gap is noisy at

at 15K), then firms at 200K where balanced exceeds standard by + 0.059 +0.059 NDCG@10 (Welch’s t t , p = 0.004 p=0.004 , n = 3 n=3 seeds per cell). At the 1M projection the 95% prediction
intervals overlap, balanced ’s lower bound ( 0.423 0.423 ) sits below standard ’s upper bound ( 0.448 0.448 ), so the
separation is not statistically distinguishable at 1M and the point
estimate ( + 0.077 +0.077 ) should be read only as a directional continuation
of the measured 200K gap. The interpretation that context
compression and document-awareness prefixes act as implicit noise
filters is therefore supported by the measured 200K result and the
monotone trend 50K → \to 200K, not by the 1M extrapolation.

blocks.en:
Projections assume (i) the log-linear relationship holds beyond 200K,
(ii) the distractor distribution remains representative of real-world
corpus growth, and (iii) the vector backend scales without
architectural changes. Assumption (i) is on empirically solid ground
for speed and standard ( R 2 ≥ 0.89 R^{2}\geq 0.89 ) but weaker
for balanced and max-reliable , whose slopes are
not distinguishable from zero, their 1M projections reflect
uncertainty about whether the flat trend will hold rather than about
the form of a decay law. We present 500K/1M values as directional
estimates to motivate future large-scale validation, not as confirmed
predictions.

blocks.en:
The SOTA-2025–2026 rerankers (Jina-v2, BGE-v2-m3, BGE-v2-gemma)
underperform on our benchmark, which we attribute to
domain-specialization: those models are tuned for web/MTEB-style
queries whereas our evaluation set blends BEIR (nfcorpus, fiqa,
scifact, arguana, hotpotqa) with QA-style prompts that favor the
older MS-MARCO-trained cross-encoders. The LLM-listwise reranker underperforms on our benchmark, with both
window settings dominated by older cross-encoders (window = 10 =10 :
NDCG@10 = 0.405 =0.405 , 2,649 2{,}649 ms; window = 5 =5 : NDCG@10 = 0.354 =0.354 , 5,441 5{,}441 ms). The window-size effect has two compounding
mechanical sources rather than a single anomaly: (i) at
window = 5 =5 , reranking the top-20 requires four sequential LLM calls
versus two at window = 10 =10 , doubling wall-clock latency before any
quality consideration;
(ii) each smaller-window call sees fewer candidates and cannot
reason globally about the ranking, a known limitation of LLM
listwise scoring that our results are consistent with rather than
novel evidence for. We tested only two window sizes on a single
93-query benchmark with one judge model, so the directional gap
should be read as confirming known LLM-listwise behavior under our
specific infrastructure rather than as a generalizable scaling claim;
a full sweep over windows ∈ { 3 , 5 , 8 , 10 , 15 , 20 } \in\{3,5,8,10,15,20\} with multiple
seeds would be needed to characterize the curve shape.

blocks.en:
Two findings emerge. First, Matryoshka truncation to 768 dimensions
( dim_768 , NDCG@10 = 0.489 =0.489 ) slightly exceeds the full
1024-dim embedding ( 0.478 0.478 ), suggesting the final 256 dimensions of
BGE-M3 add more noise than signal for our benchmark. Second, late
chunking provides a substantial uplift for BGE-large
( 0.460 → 0.493 0.460\to 0.493 , + 0.033 +0.033 ) but degrades BGE-M3
( 0.459 → 0.361 0.459\to 0.361 , − 0.098 -0.098 ). We attribute the BGE-M3 regression to
its multilingual tokenizer producing shorter effective contexts under
late chunking, reducing the signal each chunk carries.

The benefit of a stronger generator is markedly uneven. It is largest
for the lightest pipeline ( + 0.184 +0.184 ) and smallest for the heaviest
( + 0.027 +0.027 , not significant). Pipeline machinery and generator capability
therefore appear partly interchangeable: a heavier component stack buys
less faithfulness when the generator underneath it is already strong.
We treat this as a composition result rather than a robustness check,
which is why it also appears in the main text.

result honestly: this is a positional smoke run , not a
head-to-head benchmark comparison, because the only cross-framework
corpus we could stand up in the time budget is topically mismatched
to the queries it ships with.

blocks.en: H.1 Platform Isolation Verification

blocks.en:
To empirically validate lasagna ’s stage-isolation guarantees
( Section 3 ), we ran five automated tests targeting the
isolation properties that are critical for valid factorial
comparisons. Table 63 reports the results.

blocks.en:
The most critical test is session config isolation : we created
two sessions with opposite HyDE settings ( enable_hyde=True vs. False ), then verified that querying the session provider
returns the correct config for each session independently. In a naive
pipeline without session-level isolation, toggling HyDE for one
experimental configuration could leak into the next, introducing a
confound that invalidates the factorial comparison.

这混淆了因素比较的无效性。

blocks.en: H.2 Platform Showcase
blocks.zh: H.2 平台显示大小写

blocks.en:
This appendix demonstrates lasagna ’s practical usability
through code examples drawn directly from the released codebase.
We highlight five capabilities that distinguish the platform from
existing RAG toolkits: (i) a configuration UI for interactive
exploration, (ii) a layered plugin architecture with decorator-based

blocks.en: H.2.1 Configuration UI
blocks.zh: H.2.1 配置界面

blocks.en:
lasagna ships three browser-based interfaces. The
centerpiece is the RAG Configurator ( Figs. 12 and 13 ), a
profile-centric pipeline builder that lets a practitioner assemble a
working configuration without writing code or YAML. The left-hand
rail lists the four built-in profiles ( default , speed , standard , balanced , max-reliable ) alongside user-saved custom profiles, and the
main panel groups every configuration key exposed by the SDK into
four tabs, Essential, Search & Retrieval, Processing, and
Advanced, each labeled with plain-language explanations of what the
setting does, its cost implications, and the underlying YAML key
(e.g. enable_hybrid_search , enable_reranking , use_agentic_rag ). Every change is import/export-round-trippable
with the YAML contract used by the evaluation SDK
( Section H.2.5 ), so a user can prototype a profile in
the UI, export it, and run the full factorial sweep on it with no
translation. The Configurator is what gives researchers and
practitioners who are not fluent in the 127-key configuration surface
a direct path to reproducing the operational profiles in Section 5 and to iterating on them.

The other two interfaces are complementary but are not part of the public release. The Agentic Chat workspace provides
a conversational front-end with inline document management and
citation rendering; it consumes a Configurator-produced profile and
lets changes take effect on the next query without restarting the
server. The RAG Dashboard is
evaluation-oriented, with six pages (Overview, Explorer, Impact,
Pareto, Benchmark, Timeline) that visualize per-query evaluation scores. Together, the three interfaces let
a researcher configure a pipeline, run it conversationally, and
inspect its evaluation results without writing code.

blocks.en: H.2.5 Research Workflow
blocks.zh: H.2.5 研究工作

blocks.en:
Running a complete experiment requires two artifacts: a YAML
configuration file and a one-line command.

运行一个完整的实验需要两个文物: 一个YAML
配置文件和一行命令。

blocks.en:
The experiment runner handles corpus ingestion (with signature-based
caching), per-query timing, RAGAS evaluation, checkpointing, cost
tracking, and statistical testing automatically. Results are saved as
JSON with per-sample scores, enabling downstream analysis without
re-running experiments.

blocks.en:
General-purpose retrieval where precision is the primary concern:
enterprise knowledge bases, technical documentation search, and
customer support systems with moderate response times (4–7 s).
HyDE generates three hypothetical documents per query, which are
searched in parallel before cross-encoder reranking selects the top 10
passages.

精确度是主要关切的普通用途检索:
企业知识库、技术文件搜索以及
反应时间适中(4-7秒)的客户支持系统.
HyDE 每个查询生成三个假设文档,即
在交叉编码器重新排序前平行搜索
段落。

blocks.en:
Requires a vector database with hybrid (dense + BM25) search support, a
reranker model endpoint (or local GPU for mxbai-rerank-large), and one
LLM call for HyDE generation. The three HyDE variants add ∼ {\sim} 2 s of latency; operators who need to stay below 3 s can
reduce hyde_n_variants to 1 with a modest NDCG@10 reduction
( ∼ {\sim} 0.01–0.02 based on our ablation in Section 5 ).
This profile achieves the highest NDCG@10 (0.860) on the SOTA-profile
generation slice, follows the direct generation route (query routing
disabled), and enables both the hallucination and answer-quality gates
at the pipeline level. Pair it with application-level guardrails if a
per-query faithfulness floor above 0.8 0.8 is required.

blocks.en:
Recommended default for deployments that can tolerate ∼ {\sim} 12–18 s
per-query latency and require the top-band faithfulness
(batch/analyst workloads, review queues, back-office QA).
Extractive context compression reduces the token count passed to
the generator by 50 % 50\% , lowering generation cost while
preserving the most relevant spans. Document-awareness prefixes
(first 100 100 tokens) provide the generator with document-level
context at negligible additional cost. On the SOTA-profile
generation slice reported in Table 2 , balanced provides the stronger joint agentic tradeoff than max-reliable (higher NDCG@10, essentially tied
faithfulness, 13 % 13\% lower mean latency) and takes the joint
retrieval–faithfulness–latency hypervolume from standard once L ref L_{\mathrm{ref}} opens past ∼ 46 {\sim}46 s ( HV = 0.609 \mathrm{HV}{=}0.609 vs 0.579 0.579 at 60 60 s; Table 39 ). At the fixed 30 30 s reference, standard has the highest joint HV; balanced is
the appropriate choice when the application can absorb the
additional ∼ 7 {\sim}7 s of response time for
the faithfulness advantage.

blocks.en:
Infrastructure adds the agentic graph execution
( LangGraph ) to the sota_standard stack: 3 3 – 7 7 additional LLM calls per query for relevance classification,
hallucination checking, and quality gating, plus an extractive
compression step that runs locally (no additional LLM call).
Disabling MMR removes one source of latency variability without
harming retrieval quality in our experiments. End-to-end mean
latency on the SOTA slice is ∼ {\sim} 12.3 s (p95 ∼ {\sim} 26.3 s),
dominated by the agentic loop and HyDE generation. To reduce
latency, operators can disable HyDE (saving ∼ {\sim} 2–3 s) at the
cost of ∼ {\sim} 0.02 NDCG@10.

blocks.en:
High-stakes domains where answer faithfulness must be maximized and
users tolerate longer response times: medical literature review, legal
contract analysis, financial due diligence, and compliance
question-answering. The agentic pipeline performs up to three retrieval
iterations with hallucination gating; each iteration can refine or
discard unfaithful passages before the final answer is generated.
blocks.zh:
必须最大限度地加强回答忠诚的高考领域
用户容忍更长的反应时间:医学文献审查、法律
合同分析、财务尽责和遵守情况
作是问已. 代理管道最多进行三次回收
带有幻觉花纹的迭代;每个迭代可以精炼或
在生成最终答案之前丢弃不忠的段落.

blocks.en:
Infrastructure matches sota_balanced_e2e (agentic graph
execution, hybrid retrieval, reranker, HyDE) with additional
contextual retrieval and a broader chunk-cite budget (up to 30 30 retained chunks vs. 20 20 ). Both profiles share the same
agentic depth (three iterations, hallucination and answer-quality
gates enabled); the differences from sota_balanced_e2e are
retrieval-side (hybrid α = 0.3 \alpha=0.3 vs. 0.7 0.7 , contextual
retrieval enabled, wider chunk budget). Mean latency on the
SOTA-profile generation slice is ∼ {\sim} 14.2 s (p95 ∼ {\sim} 30.0 s), driven by the wider chunk pool and the agentic
loop; we recommend a concurrency limit of ∼ {\sim} 10 queries per
instance. Notably, this profile has a weaker joint tradeoff than sota_balanced_e2e within the agentic-route class on our
headline slice ( Table 2 ): faithfulness is essentially tied
( 0.916 0.916 vs 0.911 0.911 ), NDCG@10 is 0.036 0.036 lower,
and mean latency is ∼ 2 \sim{}2 s higher (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.018 p{=}0.018 ). We include it for completeness
and for deployments that require the broader retrieval envelope
(contextual retrieval, wider chunk budget) it provides.

This flowchart is derived from experiments on five BEIR domains and
may not generalize to all deployment scenarios. In particular:
(i) the MMR finding (“disable MMR”) may not hold for corpora with
genuinely redundant documents; (ii) the corpus-size threshold of 25K
is approximate and domain-dependent; (iii) absolute latency values
depend on infrastructure and will differ from our
measurements.
