blocks.en:
Several configuration comparisons in this paper differ in rank
order depending on whether the reader uses the OFAT (pooled)
reading or the hierarchical mixed-effects (query-clustered)
reading. When the two disagree by ≥ 1 {\geq}1 rank position, defer
to the hierarchical reading. It respects the query-clustering
structure ( ICC = 0.284 \text{ICC}{=}0.284 on the H1 D5 × \times D8 grid; see Section D.3 ) and is our primary inferential
position throughout the paper. The archetypal case is the H1
D5 × \times D8 attenuation: the OFAT estimate is η 2 = 0.201 \eta^{2}{=}0.201 ( p = 0.018 p{=}0.018 Holm) whereas the hierarchical LRT is χ 2 ​ ( 4 ) = 4.27 \chi^{2}(4){=}4.27 , p = 0.371 p{=}0.371 . The same pair reads as a large exploratory
interaction under OFAT and as non-significant under hierarchical
inference. The only exception is when a deployment’s per-query
variance is orthogonal to query-topic clustering (rare in practice
for benchmark corpora but possible in enterprise deployments with
strictly independent queries); in that regime the pooled OFAT
reading is closer to the deployment target. A separate, orthogonal
protocol-dependence axis (point-wise RAGAS-judge vs. pairwise
Bradley–Terry) affects within-tier configuration comparisons; see Section C.5 for the tier-vs-configuration scoping.

blocks.en: J.1 Failure–Success Taxonomy

blocks.en:
We organize root causes into a two-level taxonomy. The first level
distinguishes where in the pipeline the cause originates; the
second level identifies the mechanism by which performance is
affected. Table 67 summarizes the taxonomy with
representative examples from our experiments.

blocks.en:
This taxonomy draws on established frameworks for pipeline failure
analysis. The distinction between retrieval-side and generation-side
failures follows the “retrieve-then-read” decomposition standard in
RAG evaluation ( Gao et al., 2023b ) . The concept of functional
duplication (C1) mirrors the known subadditivity of stacked retrieval
components documented in RAG best-practice surveys ( Li et al., 2025 ) .
The diversity–relevance conflict (R2) instantiates the broader tension
between exploration and exploitation in information
retrieval ( Carbonell & Goldstein, 1998 ) .

1. Pipeline simplicity as implicit noise filter. With only 10 dense-retrieved chunks and no post-processing, the
generator receives a clean, unmodified context window. The absence
of MMR (R2), reranking reordering, and compression means the
generator sees passages in their original embedding-similarity order,
which empirically correlates with higher faithfulness
( Table 46 : speed achieves 0.991 on scifact).
This aligns with findings that simpler retrieval pipelines produce
fewer hallucinations because the generator has less opportunity to be
confused by reordered or deduplicated context ( Liu et al., 2024 ) .
Note that the speed profile does not use document awareness
(G3), its faithfulness advantage is entirely attributable to
pipeline simplicity, not to generation-side features. 2. Concise generation prompting. The speed profile uses a concise answer prompt (“Answer in ONE
sentence based only on the context”), which limits the number of
atomic claims per answer. Fewer claims mean fewer opportunities for
unsupported statements, mechanically improving RAGAS
faithfulness ( Es et al., 2024 ) . This is a measurement artifact
as much as a genuine quality improvement: a one-sentence answer with
one correct claim scores higher than a three-sentence answer with
two correct claims and one hallucinated claim.

blocks.en:
Worked Example: Why Speed Fails on Biomedical Queries (R5, Embedding Ceiling) Query (NFCorpus): “Does taking aspirin reduce the risk of colorectal cancer?” Speed profile (MiniLM-L6, dense-only, top-10): • Rank 1–3: Passages about aspirin and cardiovascular risk (cosine ≥ 0.72 \geq 0.72 ) • Rank 4–7: Passages mentioning “cancer” generically (cosine 0.65 0.65 – 0.70 0.70 ) • Rank 8–10: Off-topic passages about anti-inflammatory drugs (cosine ≈ 0.60 \approx 0.60 ) • Gold passage (aspirin + colorectal cancer meta-analysis): Rank 14 → \rightarrow missed The 384-dimensional embedding conflates “aspirin + cancer” and
“aspirin + cardiovascular” into nearby vectors. The gold passage
uses the term “chemoprevention,” which MiniLM-L6 maps far from
“reduce the risk.” Standard profile (BGE-M3, hybrid α = 0.5 \alpha{=}0.5 , reranking): • BM25 lexically matches “colorectal cancer” → \rightarrow gold passage enters
top-20 candidate set • Cross-encoder reranker promotes it to Rank 2 • Result: gold passage retrieved; NDCG@10 = 0.68 =0.68 vs. speed’s 0.31 0.31 This query illustrates three compounding failures in the speed profile:
(a) the embedding capacity ceiling prevents fine-grained biomedical
disambiguation; (b) the absence of BM25 (R5) means the exact term
“colorectal” cannot anchor retrieval; (c) no reranker means
near-misses cannot be rescued from lower ranks.

blocks.en:
Highest NDCG@10 at small scale (0.510 at 5K; 0.860 on E2E at 5.5K).
Degrades to 0.456 at 50K and 0.432 at 200K, overtaken by balanced,
with the gap becoming statistically significant only at 200K
( Δ = + 0.059 \Delta=+0.059 , p = 0.004 p=0.004 ). Faithfulness: 0.739 (E2E, 5.5K),
lower than all other SOTA profiles except Max-Reliable at scale.

1. Optimal retrieval stack for small corpora. The standard profile combines four high-impact retrieval features:
(a) cross-encoder reranking (which our ablation shows adds up to + 0.084 +0.084 NDCG@10 with the best model, ms-marco-MiniLM-L6;
the default mxbai-large used by standard provides a smaller gain, see
failure analysis below);
(b) hybrid search ( + 0.037 +0.037 ; R5 exploited);
(c) MMR disabled ( + 0.046 +0.046 ; R2 avoided);
(d) HyDE ( + 0.026 +0.026 ; R4 ).
Despite the suboptimal reranker choice, the four features jointly
lift the profile to 0.510 NDCG@10 at 5K, the highest retrieval
score among SOTA profiles, confirming that the retrieval stack is
well-chosen even if individual components are not individually
optimal ( Section D.1 ). 2. HyDE as bridging context (R4 positive mode). HyDE generates hypothetical documents that bridge the vocabulary gap
between short queries and long passages. On hotpotqa (multi-hop),
the standard profile achieves + 0.088 +0.088 NDCG@10 over the baseline
( Table 45 ), consistent with HyDE’s demonstrated
effectiveness on multi-hop queries ( Gao et al., 2023a ) . The
cross-encoder reranker acts as a noise filter for HyDE’s
occasionally hallucinated passages, preventing degradation
(R4 positive mode in the taxonomy).

blocks.en:
1. Reranker model suboptimality (R1). The standard profile uses mxbai-rerank-large-v1, which our
reranker model ablation (Exp. 15) identified as underperforming
the smaller specialist ms-marco-MiniLM-L6 on the shared 93-query
retrieval-isolation benchmark (NDCG@10 = 0.470 =0.470 vs 0.496 0.496 ,
a − 0.026 -0.026 gap; Table 51 ).
The SOTA evaluation configs retain mxbai-large because it was the
framework default and the profile configs were frozen before the
reranker comparison was conducted. Note that the reranker is a query-time knob (not in _INGESTION_TIME_KEYS ; experiment.py :60–87), so re-running with the swapped
reranker requires no re-ingestion of the corpus. The isolated
model-swap delta ( + 0.026 +0.026 ; Table 51 ) shrinks
to + 0.009 +0.009 NDCG@10 when measured end-to-end on the BEIR generation
split with the full SOTA_Std stack composed ( Table 59 ),
consistent with functional-duplication interactions (C1). The
swap remains the single easiest available improvement for the
standard profile. 2. Scale fragility (C3). The standard profile degrades log-linearly at − 0.055 -0.055 NDCG/decade
( R 2 = 0.895 R^{2}=0.895 , p = 0.004 p=0.004 ), a 3.7 × 3.7\times steeper slope than
balanced ( − 0.015 -0.015 /decade; slope not distinguishable from zero, p = 0.175 p=0.175 ; Table 23 ).
The root cause is the absence of generation-side defenses:
without context compression (G2) or document awareness (G3), the
generator receives 5 full-length passages (up to 4,000 tokens)
whose relevance quality degrades as corpus size increases.
At 50K documents, the proportion of near-miss distractors in the
top-20 candidate set increases, and without compression to distil
the most relevant spans, the generator is more likely to attend to
irrelevant context. This mechanism is consistent with the
“lost in the middle” phenomenon ( Liu et al., 2024 ) , where
generators struggle to utilize relevant information when it is
embedded in a long, partially irrelevant context window. 3. No faithfulness safeguards. The standard profile achieves the lowest faithfulness among SOTA
profiles (0.739 at 5.5K; Table 2 ). Without agentic
quality gates (G1), hallucination checks, or context compression
(G2), the generator operates on raw retrieved context with no
verification layer. The faithfulness ANOVA shows that query
augmentation and agentic gating together explain η 2 = 0.191 \eta^{2}=0.191 of faithfulness variance ( Section 5 ), variance that
the standard profile cannot capture because it lacks both
components.

blocks.en:
Worked Example: How HyDE Helps and Hurts on Multi-Hop Queries (R4) Query (HotpotQA): “The Soul of Buddha is a 1918 American
silent romance film shot in a borough that…” This multi-hop query requires bridging two facts: (1) the film’s
shooting location, and (2) properties of that location. The original
query text contains no entity name for the borough. Without HyDE (dense-only retrieval): • Top-20 results: passages about 1918 films, silent cinema, romance
genre, none about the specific borough • NDCG@10 = 0.22 =0.22 (no bridging passage retrieved) With HyDE (3 hypothetical documents): • HyDE generates: “The Soul of Buddha (1918) was filmed in Fort
Lee, New Jersey, a borough known for its early film studios…” • The hypothetical document introduces “Fort Lee”, a plausible
(and correct) entity that anchors dense retrieval • Gold passage about Fort Lee enters top-20; reranker promotes it to Rank 3 • NDCG@10 = 0.61 =0.61 ( + 0.39 +0.39 from HyDE bridging) HyDE failure mode (same query, balanced profile without reranker): • One of the 3 HyDE variants hallucinates: “…filmed in
Brooklyn, a densely populated borough…” • Without the reranker to filter, the Brooklyn passage ranks above
the Fort Lee passage → \rightarrow wrong context reaches the generator • This explains R4’s profile-dependence: HyDE helps when a reranker
is present to filter hallucinated variants ( − 0.031 -0.031 dropout in
Max-Reliable), but can propagate noise without one ( + 0.008 +0.008 dropout in balanced)

blocks.en:
The standard profile is optimally designed for small-corpus,
retrieval-focused deployments where generation quality is less
critical. Its scale fragility is a direct consequence of its
retrieval-only optimization strategy: the features that maximize NDCG@10
at 5K (HyDE, reranking) do not address the generation-side challenges

Worked Example: Document Awareness Grounds a Financial Query (G3) Query (FiQA): “Opening a Roth IRA account, what is the fee
structure for Vanguard vs. Scottrade?” Without document awareness (standard profile): • Top-5 reranked chunks: 3 about Vanguard fees, 2 about brokerage
accounts generically • Generator sees 5 passage fragments with no file-level context • Generated answer discusses Vanguard fees accurately but hallucinates a Scottrade fee schedule (Scottrade chunk at Rank 8,
outside top-10) • Faithfulness: 0.67 (one claim unsupported) With 100-token prefix (balanced profile): • Each chunk is prefixed with the first 100 tokens of its source document: “ [Vanguard_fee_schedule.pdf] Vanguard offers several
types of IRA accounts including Traditional, Roth, and SEP…” • The generator can now distinguish which document each chunk originates
from and recognize that no Scottrade document is present in the context • Generated answer correctly states Vanguard fees and notes that
insufficient information is available for Scottrade • Faithfulness: 1.00 The 100-token prefix costs only + 15 +15 ms but enables the generator to
reason about source provenance , which documents are present and,
critically, which are absent. Longer prefixes (300 tokens) dilute this
signal with boilerplate, explaining the diminishing returns observed in
Exp. 17 (0.411 at 100 tokens vs. 0.347 at 300 tokens).

blocks.en: Faithfulness: 1.00

4. Scale robustness from generation-side defenses (C3 mitigated). The combination of compression and document awareness provides
two independent defenses against scale-induced degradation:
compression filters noisy passages, and awareness provides
document-level context that remains informative even when individual
chunks become less relevant. The balanced profile’s degradation
slope ( − 0.015 -0.015 NDCG/decade, not significantly different from zero, p = 0.175 p=0.175 ) is 3.7 × 3.7\times flatter than standard’s ( − 0.055 -0.055 , p = 0.004 p=0.004 ), directly attributable to these features.
On E2E faithfulness, balanced maintains 0.935 at 50K vs. standard’s 0.793, a + 0.142 +0.142 gap that widens with scale. 5. Composition penalty minimized by complementary features. Unlike the Max-Reliable profile (which stacks overlapping features),
balanced’s additions (compression, awareness) operate on different pipeline stages than its retrieval features.
Compression acts on the output of reranking (post-retrieval);
awareness acts on the generation prompt (pre-generation). Neither
duplicates the function of HyDE, reranking, or hybrid search.
The dropout analysis ( Section D.12 ) confirms this
complementarity: removing compression from balanced costs only − 0.006 -0.006 NDCG@10, and removing document awareness costs − 0.055 -0.055 ,
while removing the reranker costs − 0.072 -0.072 , each feature’s dropout
delta is close to its single-feature ablation delta, indicating
minimal interference. By contrast, the full five-feature stack
( Section D.14 ) incurs a 72% composition penalty
precisely because retrieval-side features overlap in function.

4.四. 由生成侧防(C3减轻)而来的规模强性. 压缩与文档意识相结合
防止由规模引起的退化的两项独立辩护:
压缩过滤器会发出噪音,
即使在个人情况下仍然提供信息的文档级别上下文
块变得不那么重要。 平衡面貌的退化
坡度(− 0.015-0.015 NDCG/十年,与零没有显著区别,p=0.175 p=0.175)为3.7×3.7相乘以标准相乘(0.055-0.055,p=0.004 p=0.04),可直接归因于这些特征.
在E2E的忠诚度上,平衡维持了0.935,在50K对标准为0.793,一个+0.142+0.142的相差会随着尺度而扩大. 5. 以补充性特征尽量减少构成处罚。 与Max-Reliable配置文件不同(它堆叠了相重叠的特性),
平衡的添加(压缩、意识)在不同的管道阶段运作,与其检索功能不同。
重排输出的压抑行为(回收后);
意识作用于生成时(生成前)。 也没有
重复 HyDE 、 重新排序或混合搜索的功能。
辍学分析(D.12节)证实了这一点。
互补性:仅去除平衡成本的压缩-0.006-0.006 NDCG@10,并去除文件宣传成本-0.055-0.055,
在去除重排成本时 - 0.072 - 0.072, 每个特性的退出
三角洲接近其单一地貌的萎缩三角洲,表明
最小的干扰。 反之,整个五地层堆放
(D.14节)处以72%的组成处罚
这正是因为检索-侧功能在功能上的重叠.

blocks.en:
The balanced profile’s strong agentic tradeoff arises from a principled
design: it exhausts the retrieval stack (where the largest gains are
available) and adds generation-side defenses that address different failure modes (noise filtering, context grounding) rather than
amplifying the same capability. This complementary design minimizes
the composition penalty and provides scale robustness that
retrieval-only profiles lack.

blocks.en:
1. Aggressive refinement paradox (G1 negative mode). The agentic pipeline’s chunk refinement classifies 13–14 of 15
retrieved chunks as “not relevant” on multi-hop queries,
discarding evidence that the generator needs for comprehensive
answers. When all chunks are discarded, a single fallback chunk
is returned. This starves the generator: with one chunk of ∼ 800 {\sim}800 tokens, the answer is necessarily incomplete.
The dropout analysis confirms this: removing agentic RAG from
the Max-Reliable base profile improves NDCG@10 by + 0.021 +0.021 ( Table 44 ). Separately, the cross-profile comparison
shows E2E exact match at 0.163 (standard) vs. 0.101
(Max-Reliable), consistent with reduced answer completeness. Mechanistic detail. The refinement uses an LLM judge to classify each chunk as relevant , partially_relevant , or not_relevant . The judge operates on individual chunks
without cross-chunk context, so a chunk that provides necessary bridging evidence for a multi-hop query may be classified as
not relevant because it does not directly answer the query. This is
consistent with the pointwise scoring approach used in passage
reranking ( Nogueira & Cho, 2019 ) , where each passage is
evaluated independently; the effect is amplified when the refinement
threshold is aggressive (our default: only relevant chunks
pass).

blocks.en:
Worked Example: The Aggressive Refinement Paradox on a Multi-Hop Query (G1) Query (MuSiQue): “In what part of Florida is Tom Denney’s
birthplace located?” This query decomposes into two hops: (1) Where was Tom Denney born?
(2) What part of Florida is that city in? Retrieval (shared across balanced and Max-Reliable): top-15
chunks include: C1 “Tom Denney (born 1982) is a guitarist from
Coral Springs, Florida…” hop 1: birthplace C4 “Coral Springs is a city in Broward County,
in the southeastern part of the state…” hop 2: location C7 “Denney was the lead guitarist and a founding
member of A Day to Remember…” biographical context C9–C15 Various passages about Florida cities, other musicians
from Florida distractors Max_reliable refinement (3-iteration agentic pipeline): • Iteration 1 : LLM judge classifies each chunk independently against the query • C1 → \rightarrow partially_relevant (mentions birthplace but not “part of Florida”) • C4 → \rightarrow not_relevant (discusses Coral Springs geography
but does not mention Tom Denney) • C7 → \rightarrow not_relevant (biography, no location info) • C9–C15 → \rightarrow not_relevant • Result : 14/15 chunks discarded. Only C1 passes (downgraded
from partially_relevant by the strict threshold).
Fallback: 1 chunk returned. Generated answers : • Balanced (all 5 reranked chunks passed to generator): “Tom Denney was born in Coral Springs, which is in the
southeastern part of Florida.” → \rightarrow Correct, both hops answered. Faithfulness: 1.0, EM: 1. • Max_reliable (1 fallback chunk, C1 only): “Tom Denney was born in Coral Springs, Florida.” → \rightarrow Partially correct, birthplace is stated but “part of
Florida” is missing (C4 was discarded). Faithfulness: 1.0 (answer
is grounded), but EM: 0 (incomplete). The paradox: Max-Reliable achieves higher faithfulness (the
answer is fully grounded in the single chunk it kept) but lower answer completeness (it cannot answer the second hop). The pointwise
judge cannot recognize that C4 is essential bridging evidence
because C4 alone says nothing about Tom Denney.

2. Latency cost without proportional quality gain. The agentic pipeline adds 3–7 LLM calls per query (planning,
per-chunk relevance classification, hallucination check, quality
gate, optional re-retrieval). Each call adds ∼ 1 {\sim}1 –3 s via
the API gateway, contributing to the + 2.0 +2.0 s p95 latency increase
over balanced. The faithfulness gain ( + 0.005 +0.005 over balanced) does
not justify this cost for most applications, making the profile
less efficient on the joint tradeoff. 3. Composition penalty from feature stacking (C1). Max_reliable activates everything that balanced has plus agentic components. But the agentic pipeline partially duplicates
the function of context compression: both reduce the context to

and explicitly disables query expansion and RAG fusion, features

blocks.en: J.3 Cross-Profile Interaction Analysis

blocks.en:
The per-profile analyses above identify several recurring interaction
patterns. We consolidate these into three principal interaction
mechanisms, each grounded in the factorial ANOVA and DID probes.

blocks.en: J.3.1 Interaction I1: Embedding × \times Enrichment
blocks.zh: J.3.1 相互作用 I1: 嵌入X-时间浓缩

blocks.en:

blocks.en:
Enrichment methods (contextual retrieval, RAPTOR) prepend synthetic
context to document chunks before embedding. The quality of the
resulting embedding depends on how well the embedding model can encode
this prepended context: • High-capacity embedders (E5-large, BGE-M3, 1024d):
The additional context provides useful signal, and the model has
sufficient capacity to encode it. However, our results show that
even with high-capacity embedders, enrichment does not improve over
the none baseline ( η enrichment 2 = 0.144 \eta^{2}_{\text{enrichment}}=0.144 , best
level: none). This suggests that on domain-focused corpora, the
original document text already provides sufficient embedding signal. • Low-capacity embedders (MiniLM-L6, 384d):
The prepended context overwhelms the model’s limited representational
capacity, diluting the embedding of the original text. This produces
a negative interaction: enrichment hurts more with weaker
embedders.

blocks.en: J.3.2 Interaction I2: Embedding × \times Reranking
blocks.zh: J.3.2 交互 I2: 嵌入 \ times 重排

blocks.en:
Cross-encoder rerankers operate on (query, passage) pairs and produce
calibrated relevance scores. Their effectiveness depends on the
quality of the candidate set provided by the first-stage retriever: • Strong first-stage retrieval (BGE-M3 + hybrid):
The candidate set already contains mostly relevant passages; the
reranker refines their ordering but has limited room for
improvement. The marginal gain of reranking is moderate. • Weak first-stage retrieval (MiniLM-L6, dense-only):
The candidate set contains more noise; the reranker can rescue
relevant passages from lower ranks, providing a larger marginal
gain. This produces a compensatory interaction: reranking benefits
weaker embedders more than stronger ones. The practical consequence is
that practitioners with strong embeddings should invest less in
reranking and more in other dimensions (compression, awareness).

blocks.en: J.3.3 Interaction I3: Query Augmentation × \times Agentic Gate
blocks.zh: J.3.3 互动 I3: 查询增强 ×\times 代理门

blocks.en:
η 2 = 0.191 \eta^{2}=0.191 (Type-III; raw η 2 = 0.259 \eta^{2}=0.259 ), F ⁡ ( 12,279 ) = 5.47 F(12,279)=5.47 , p < 0.001 p<0.001 on faithfulness; Holm-adjusted p = 0.018 p=0.018 (122 configs; Section 5 ). This is the strongest interaction on
faithfulness and near the pre-registered H1 threshold ( η 2 = 0.20 \eta^{2}=0.20 ).

Query augmentation (HyDE, RAG fusion) expands the retrieval input,
producing a richer but noisier candidate set. The agentic gate
(CRAG, self-RAG, speculative RAG) filters this candidate set by
evaluating each passage’s support for the generated answer: • Augmentation alone (no gating): Noisy candidates
pass through to the generator, which may hallucinate from
irrelevant passages. Faithfulness does not improve ( Δ = 0.00 \Delta=0.00 for RAG fusion; Section D.1 ). • Gating alone (no augmentation): The gate filters a
standard candidate set, which may already be insufficient.
Faithfulness improves modestly ( Δ = + 0.05 \Delta=+0.05 for agentic RAG). • Augmentation + gating : The enriched candidate set
provides the gate with more material to work with; the gate filters
aggressively, leaving only high-confidence passages. The combined
effect is superadditive: the gate’s precision increases because
augmentation provides better recall.

blocks.en:
This is the only positive (superadditive) interaction we observe;
all other significant interactions are subadditive (composition
penalty). It operates across the retrieval–generation boundary,
confirming that the composition problem manifests asymmetrically:
within-stage interactions are typically subadditive (overlapping
function), while cross-stage interactions can be synergistic
(complementary function).

确认构成问题表现不对称:
阶段内的互动通常是次辅助(重叠)
函数),而跨阶段互动可以协同
(辅助职能)。

blocks.en:
Worked Example: Augmentation + Gating Synergy on a SciFact Claim (I3) Query (SciFact): “Basophils counteract disease development
in patients with systemic lupus.” This claim-verification query requires retrieving passages that
directly support or refute a specific biomedical assertion. No augmentation, no gating HyDE augmentation + agentic gating Dense retrieval returns 5 passages about basophils and lupus, 2
relevant, 3 tangential (general immunology). HyDE generates a hypothetical passage elaborating on basophil-mediated
immune regulation → \rightarrow retrieves 8 candidates including 4
relevant and 4 tangential. Generator uses all 5 unfiltered. Produces answer citing one tangential
passage → \rightarrow one unsupported claim. Agentic gate evaluates all 8: keeps only the 4 that directly discuss
basophils in lupus contexts. Discards 4 tangential. Faithfulness: 0.75 Generator receives 4 high-relevance passages → \rightarrow every claim
grounded. Faithfulness: 1.0 Why this
is superadditive : HyDE alone would add noisy candidates that reduce
faithfulness (net Δ = 0.00 \Delta=0.00 ). Gating alone filters the original
5 passages but cannot improve recall beyond what dense retrieval
provides ( Δ = + 0.05 \Delta=+0.05 ). Together, HyDE provides the richer
candidate pool that the gate needs to select from, while the gate
removes the noise that HyDE introduces, each component compensates
for the other’s weakness.

blocks.en: J.4 Scaling Root Causes
blocks.zh: J.4 扩大根源

blocks.en:
The corpus scaling experiments ( Section 5 ) reveal two
phenomena that require mechanistic explanation: (1) log-linear
degradation for retrieval-side profiles ( speed , standard ) contrasted with effectively flat behavior for
generation-oriented profiles ( balanced , max-reliable ), and (2) a rank crossover between standard and balanced that is visible from 25K and
statistically significant at 200K ( p = 0.004 p=0.004 ).

需要机械解释的现象: (1) 对数线

面向生成的剖面图(平衡,最大可靠),以及(2) 标准与平衡之间的分级交叉,从25K和
统计意义为200K (p = 0.004 p = 0.004)。

blocks.en:
As corpus size increases from 5K to 50K documents, distractor density
in the candidate set increases proportionally. For a fixed top- k k retrieval, the probability that a given candidate slot is occupied by a
distractor increases as 1 − R / N 1-R/N , where R R is the number of relevant
documents and N N is the corpus size. Since R R is fixed (the same
queries target the same documents), the signal-to-noise ratio in the
candidate set degrades logarithmically with N N .

分心器随着1-R / N 1-R / N 增加,其中R 为相关数目

The degradation rate varies by profile because different features
provide different levels of noise robustness: • Speed ( − 0.115 -0.115 /decade, R 2 = 0.90 R^{2}=0.90 ): No noise filtering;
degradation rate matches the raw retriever’s sensitivity to distractors. • Standard ( − 0.055 -0.055 /decade, R 2 = 0.89 R^{2}=0.89 ): HyDE and reranking
provide partial noise filtering, but the reranker sees the same degraded
candidate set. • Balanced ( − 0.015 -0.015 /decade): Context compression and
document awareness provide generation-side noise filtering that is independent of candidate set quality; even when the retriever
returns noisier candidates, compression distils the relevant spans. • Max reliable : Not measured at 50K due to computational
budget, but the agentic pipeline’s iterative refinement provides
an additional noise filter.

blocks.en:
The standard profile’s advantage over balanced at 5K ( + 0.006 +0.006 NDCG@10)
reverses between 15K and 25K. The gap trends in the predicted
direction at 50K–100K but is not statistically significant through
100K ( p > 0.17 p>0.17 , Welch’s t t , n = 3 n=3 seeds per cell); it firms at
200K ( Δ = + 0.059 \Delta=+0.059 ; p = 0.004 p=0.004 ). The root cause is the
asymmetric scaling of retrieval-side vs. generation-side
defenses: • Retrieval-side defenses (HyDE, reranking) operate on
the candidate set, whose quality degrades with scale. HyDE’s
hypothetical documents are generated from the query, not the corpus,
so they do not adapt to increasing distractor density. The
reranker scores each candidate independently, so its effectiveness
degrades linearly with the fraction of distractors in the
candidate set. • Generation-side defenses (compression, awareness)
operate on the output of retrieval, after reranking has already
selected the top-10. Even when these top-10 passages contain more
noise at scale, compression can extract the relevant spans, and
document awareness provides stable grounding that does not degrade
with corpus size.

blocks.en:
This analysis provides causal support for the H3 hypothesis premise:
profile rankings are not scale-invariant because different features
have different scaling slopes. A profile optimized for small-scale
retrieval (standard) will be overtaken by a profile with better
generation-side defenses (balanced) as scale increases.

有不同的缩放坡度。 小规模配置优化
检索( 标准) 将被更好的配置文件所取代
随着规模的增加,生成方防御(平衡).

blocks.en:
Three actionable principles emerge from this root cause analysis: 1. Complement, don’t duplicate. Features that operate on different pipeline stages (retrieval vs. generation) compose better than features within the same stage.
The balanced profile exemplifies this by pairing retrieval features
(HyDE, reranking, hybrid) with generation features (compression,
awareness). 2. Validate composed configurations end-to-end. Single-feature ablations consistently overestimate composed
performance (composition penalties of 7–72% are observed; Section 5 ). The only reliable guide is factorial
evaluation of the composed system. 3. Choose features for your scale. Retrieval-side features (HyDE, reranking) provide the largest
gains at small scale ( < < 10K documents) but degrade faster.
Generation-side features (compression, awareness) provide smaller
gains initially but maintain their effectiveness at scale.
Profile selection should account for the target corpus size.

blocks.en:
This appendix catalogs the techniques associated with the eight
component dimensions varied in the factorial experiment. These
dimensions sit within the nine-stage workflow described in Section 3 : document processing and the base answer generator
were held fixed, while D8 varies agentic control around generation.
Practitioners seeking implementation details for any method can refer
to the cited papers; our implementations follow the original
algorithms unless noted.

blocks.en: K.1 Embedding Models (D1)
blocks.zh: K.1 嵌入模型(D1)

blocks.en:
all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim) A lightweight sentence-transformer distilled from
MiniLM ( Wang et al., 2020 ) via knowledge distillation on 1B
sentence pairs. Fast inference ( ∼ {\sim} 10K sentences/s on GPU)
at the cost of lower representation capacity. Used in the speed profile. BAAI/bge-m3 (1024-dim) A unified embedding model supporting dense, sparse (lexical
weights), and ColBERT-style multi-vector
retrieval ( Chen et al., 2024a ) . Trained on multilingual data
with 8K context window. Our default embedding for all non-speed
profiles. intfloat/e5-large-v2 (1024-dim) A text embedding model trained with contrastive learning on
large-scale text pairs, achieving strong performance on the MTEB
benchmark ( Wang et al., 2022 ) . BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 (1024-dim) An English-focused embedding model from the BGE
family ( Xiao et al., 2024 ) , optimized for retrieval via

blocks.en: K.2 Chunking Strategies (D2)
blocks.zh: K.2 弹簧策略( D2)

blocks.en:
Fixed-size chunking Splits documents into fixed-length segments (512 tokens in our
experiments) with configurable overlap. Simple and deterministic. Semantic chunking Groups consecutive sentences whose embeddings are within a
similarity threshold, producing semantically coherent
chunks ( Chen et al., 2024b ) . Chunk boundaries align with topic
shifts. Sentence-window chunking Each chunk centers on a single sentence but includes a
configurable window of surrounding sentences as context.
Preserves local coherence while maintaining fine-grained retrieval
units. Hierarchical chunking Creates parent chunks (2000 tokens) containing child chunks
(400 tokens). Retrieval operates on children; auto-merge
promotes to parents when multiple children from the same parent
are retrieved, recovering broader context ( Sarthi et al., 2024 ) . Structure-aware chunking Splits documents along structural boundaries extracted during
document parsing (headings, sections, tables, code blocks)
rather than by fixed token counts. Preserves layout semantics
from the source format (Markdown, HTML, PDF) and
keeps related structural units, table rows, list items, code
blocks, in a single chunk; parsed via
Docling ( Auer et al., 2024 ) . Recursive chunking Splits documents hierarchically using a prioritized list of
separators (paragraph → \to sentence → \to clause → \to token),
recursively subdividing any segment that exceeds the target
chunk size. Produces variable-length chunks that respect
natural text boundaries while bounding chunk size, a pattern
popularized by LangChain and LlamaIndex as the default
general-purpose splitter.

sparse baseline in our executable comparisons

hybrid retrieval modes below. SPLADE (learned sparse) A learned sparse expansion model ( Formal et al., 2021 ; Formal et al., 2022 ) that produces weighted term vectors by expanding queries and
documents over a BERT vocabulary, enabling lexical match on
semantically related terms. Hybrid-BM25 Combines dense retrieval with BM25 lexical
matching ( Robertson & Zaragoza, 2009 ) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion
(RRF) ( Cormack et al., 2009 ) . The fusion weight α \alpha controls the dense–sparse balance. Hybrid-SPLADE Replaces BM25 with SPLADE ( Formal et al., 2021 ) , combined
with dense retrieval via RRF. Hybrid (RRF fusion) Reciprocal Rank Fusion ( Cormack et al., 2009 ; Bruch et al., 2023 ) is the rank-aggregation algorithm that underlies all lasagna hybrid modes: each result list contributes a
score 1 / ( k + r i ) 1/(k+r_{i}) for document at rank r i r_{i} (we use the
standard k = 60 k=60 ), and the fused ranking sorts by summed score.
Robust to per-retriever score scales and the default fusion

extracted at index time. For a query, entities and neighbors
within k k hops are materialized as additional passages
alongside the top- k k vector hits, broadening recall on
multi-hop questions ( Edge et al., 2024 ) . Shares the
ingestion pipeline with the GraphRAG enrichment
( GraphRAG ) and was excluded from the
factorial on cost grounds ( Section A.4 ).

blocks.en:
A parallel line of work replaces flat vector retrieval with graph-
or schema-based indexes: HippoRAG ( Gutiérrez et al., 2024 ) runs
personalized PageRank over an entity graph, KAG ( Liang et al., 2024 ) fuses schema-aware knowledge-graph traversal with a semantic layer,
and hierarchical extensions such as TreeRAG ( Tao et al., 2025 ) add document-tree structure. These systems are complementary to lasagna : each replaces the retrieval-stage internals while
preserving the stage-isolation interface, so they can be dropped in
as an additional D4 (retrieval) level and evaluated under the same
factorial protocol. We did not include them in the 242-cell design
because the D-optimal set was locked at pre-registration; a natural
extension is to test whether graph-based indexing changes the
D5 × \times D8 composition patterns reported in Table 42 .

和分级扩展,如TreatyRAG(Tao等,2025年)会添加文档-树结构. 这些系统与千层面条互为补充:每个系统都取代取回阶段的内部,同时

作为额外的D4(检索)职等,并在同一项目下进行评估

blocks.en:
None The original query is used as-is for retrieval. HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings) An LLM generates hypothetical answer documents; their embeddings
are averaged with the query embedding to improve recall for
underspecified queries ( Gao et al., 2023a ) . RAG-Fusion Generates multiple query variants via an LLM, retrieves for each,
and merges results via RRF ( Rackauckas, 2024 ) .
Broadens the retrieval scope at the cost of additional LLM calls. Query decomposition Decomposes complex queries into sub-questions, retrieves for each,
and aggregates evidence. Effective for multi-hop
reasoning ( Press et al., 2023 ) . Step-back prompting Generates a more abstract “step-back” question that captures
the high-level intent, retrieves for both the original and
abstracted queries ( Zheng et al., 2024 ) .

the same agentic graph as the quality-gate filter.

blocks.en:
The evaluation uses one constructed English multi-domain test bed, at most 93
retrieval queries and 200 generation queries per experiment, in five focused
domains. It does not test multilingual corpora, real enterprise or private data,
open-weight generators, or cross-organizational large corpora. Faithfulness is
measured under two generator models, a sensitivity check rather than a sweep,
and absolute faithfulness scores rest on one judge’s calibration
( Limitations , after Section 6 ).

blocks.en: L.3 Where This Work Sits
blocks.zh: L.3 工作地点

blocks.en:
The paper sits between RAG methods research ( Lewis et al., 2020 ; Gao et al., 2023b ) ,
RAG evaluation frameworks and metrics ( Es et al., 2024 ; Saad-Falcon et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2024 ) ,
retrieval benchmarking ( Thakur et al., 2021 ) , toolkits that compose RAG
pipelines ( Jin et al., 2025 ; Rau et al., 2024 ) or search over
them ( Kim et al., 2024 ) , and the design of experiments for comparing many
configurations ( Montgomery, 2021 ; Fedorov et al., 1972 ) . Its contribution
is a measurement of how techniques compose, not a new technique.
